EMERALD CHAMPIONS — THE GAME AND BATTLE BOOK, V4
================================================

Single editable working specification • updated September 13, 2026
Source foundation: Emerald Champions 7.1, 2f05b7a6f18ead96a0f81d4d6c73b28852a10150, plus the isolated book-implementation work. This file is the current design authority. Historical editions and the supplied trainer-review HTML are evidence, not competing active books.

V4 consolidates one continuous story, explicit guide-free directions at every required handoff, planned overworld sequences, the existing exact game systems/data, and the trainer audit. The latest user decisions require the designated story chapters in sequence and authorize the AI to read the player's committed moves and targets. There is no separate optional research track.

STATUS: v4 implementation and earned native playthrough are in progress. The single Astra High review is complete and integrated; do not repeat it. The retained roster, individual legendary caps, shared committed-player-command AI and substantial systems/scene work are implemented. The fresh Medium campaign has 35 earned unique trainer clears and has reached C13; Cristian was beaten on attempt three after two losses. Jocelyn was beaten on attempt three in seven turns after losses of 13 and eight turns; Brawly remains undefeated. C13 Ring/manor handoffs and all later chapters still require earned traversal and encounter-by-encounter review. Implemented code and selected passing fixtures do not certify the full story, AI quality, timing, balance or user visual acceptance. Repository docs/CONTINUE.md owns the exact resumption checkpoint and evidence index; this book owns game design. The full game goal remains unfinished.

DESIGN rules govern intended behavior. Preserved SEED records are the explicitly inherited baseline where no design amendment overrides them. Exact trainer data, habitats, evolution relationships, shop/gift dispositions, all 99 Mega types and map identities remain in this file. Detailed engine code, pixel assets and unchanged flavor dialogue stay in the source; they are not falsely claimed to be reproduced byte for byte here.

The goal is a complete and coherent specification that makes implementation clear. Text review does not prove native mechanics, difficulty, performance, reachable maps or correct rendering. Those remain explicit acceptance work. The one authorized fresh Astra High full-context review has already run, its findings were reported and integrated in section 26, and the user subsequently stopped subagent work. No additional agent or repeated review loop is authorized.

1. THE GAME AND THE ROSTER
==========================

We are designing a long, cohesive Hoenn adventure whose highest release setting aspires to exceptional strategic doubles difficulty. The comparison with Emerald Kaizo is a target for player testing, not a claim already proved. The player should finish with real understanding of speed control, partner support, targeting, switching, terrain/weather, protection and disruption.

Easy/Medium/Hard remain GLOBAL TRAINER-LEVEL calibration controls during development. They do not change the player cap, teams, AI quality or story. Retain all three development controls; select final release labels after playtesting without changing this level-only contract.

Roster starting ranges are approximately 650–750 obtainable species, 300–400 direct ordinary wild-table species, and 300–400 purposeful opponent showcase species. These are hypotheses, not quotas. A wild Ralts-family opportunity can yield multiple player options and several trainer stages; therefore equal wild/showcase numbers do not mean every wild slot needs its own trainer. Cosmetic/transient forms do not inflate the ordinary species target. Functional regional forms and Megas get explicit records.

The current seed has 654 exact wild-table identities and 791 exact authored opponent identities, including forms. These are NOT directly comparable National Dex counts. Keep 7.1's actual distribution until a family-by-family decision justifies a change. Preserve route identity, sensible progression and useful early options; do not flood early routes with later signature species merely to align a stone.

KEEP reasons: supported Mega family; selected legendary/story role; meaningful historical competitive relevance; distinctive doubles function; loved/nostalgic identity; habitat or early-evolution value. Obscurity alone is not a cut reason. A weak favorite can stay; a redundant attacker with no identity can go. The initial 290-entry watchlist below is an editable selection, not an objective popularity ranking or a completed audit of every past format.

Representation has THREE independent questions:
1. Can the player obtain it and its selected evolutions/forms?
2. Does it have a memorable encounter, including a legendary's own battle?
3. Does the chosen trainer-showcase roster give it a meaningful opponent role?
A Mew capture scene need not also force Mew onto an unrelated passenger. Do not assign missing names to arbitrary spare slots just to close a count.

Wild revision method: keep habitat and map/method structure; select/remove families only with a stated reason; consolidate redundant stages only where it improves discovery; preserve rare-find identity without mandatory RNG gates. Whenever a family changes, review its evolution item, Mega, trades/gifts, field capabilities, local dialogue and opposing showcases in the same record.


KARTANA — EXPLICIT PRESERVATION DECISION
Keep Kartana accessible through the existing M529 PetalburgWoods3 route and its 8% ordinary-wild table/provider. Do not add a badge/story lock, lower its encounter weight or remove it merely because it is strong or classified as exceptional. Physical-access/obstacle/marker checks remain necessary to ensure the intended route works; those checks are NOT authorization to gate it later. Preserve the rest of the 7.1 habitat template.

Trainer roster: the reviewed v4 target is 342 distinct authored trainer battles across 324 active E groups and 369 party definitions. The first implementation pass retired 140 ordinary/casual groups (142 identities); v4 additionally retires four whole groups and one of E0130’s two fights, including three redundant story grunts and two reporter stages. All named bosses, important rivals, Gym personnel and League identities remain. These five additional removals are implemented in the current authored roster and native entry sites; current book/team materialization contains 369 party definitions. Their full campaign consequences still require earned traversal. The count is not the number of unavoidable fights on a played route; see section 8.


2. CAMPAIGN AND CAPS — DESIGN
=============================

The Gym journey, Magma/Aqua conflict and added areas form the continuous story below. Story completion, optional capture and physical reward delivery have distinct outcomes. Victory/capture can resolve a designated encounter; fleeing/loss does not. Storage failure cannot block reporting, and a failed catch must retain a later opportunity.

Cap increases occur AFTER the stated milestone, never halfway through its required boss. Party acquisitions are normalized DOWN to the current player cap if necessary; the free Leveler can raise a weaker gift. Ordinary evolution does not raise a Pokémon above its cap. Release-label selection does not change this cap contract.

For a Normal design baseline, ordinary trainer members sit around cap−2 to cap, strong expedition/rival members around cap to cap+1, and bosses mostly cap+1/+2 with an occasional +3 ace. Easy/Hard development offsets start at −2/+2 relative to that baseline. FINAL LEVEL = clamp(live player cap + member role offset + development offset, 1, 100), except the bespoke pre-preparation rescue. Story prerequisites determine a required boss’s expected first-fight cap. Old 7.1 authored absolute levels are discarded in the planned game, including the old level-98–100 ferry teams. If a late offset reaches 100 it stops there; no hidden stat multiplier replaces the lost offset.

All ordinary/optional trainer baselines use the LIVE player cap, so early access or a later return never inherits an arbitrary old level-100 floor. Mandatory boss milestones determine the expected live cap at their first fight. First-time mandatory encounter counts remain separate from optional replays. Opening rescue uses bespoke low levels before preparation; the first prepared rival can use the opening cap. No team can be tuned simply by pretending all players already selected one specific counter.

LEGENDARY BASE-STAT CAP — USER-APPROVED DIRECTION
Player-owned legendary and mythical species/forms above 600 configured base-stat total use an individual level cap: max(1, floor(chapter cap × 600 / BST)). Species at or below 600 keep the full chapter cap. The 600 benchmark is the high end of ordinary fully evolved Pokémon, including pseudo-legendaries. Use the actual configured game stats, not an external unmodified dex or a fixed five-percent penalty. This replaces the earlier proposed 95-percent trial; no one-restricted-slot rule is imposed and stacking does not add a second cumulative penalty.
At chapter cap 100, Kyogre's 670 BST gives level 89, Mewtwo's 680 gives 88, and Arceus's 720 gives 83. A later discussion about reducing even 600-BST legendary species and removing the penalty after Champion was discussion only; no change was approved. The implemented policy in this paragraph remains current. Their moves, typing, abilities, stat distribution, nature, IVs and EVs remain intact. This normalizes approximate overall raw stats, not every individual stat or guaranteed battle strength. Levels also affect damage, so native outcome/pacing tests must assess the real consequences.
Use the configured legendary/sublegendary/mythical classifications and the stable species/form the player owns. Weak pre-evolutions and ordinary 600-BST legends receive no reduction. Ultra Beasts and Paradox Pokémon are not automatically a restricted category; Kartana's existing access and ordinary 570-BST cap remain unchanged. Persistent fusions/rider forms use their own BST. Temporary Mega/Primal/Gigantamax/Tera/Ultra forms do not cause a second midbattle level adjustment; their normal transformation mechanics remain intact.
The chapter cap remains the progression/money and trainer-authoring baseline. Opposing trainer and wild encounter levels keep their explicit existing rules; this is the PLAYER preparation/acquisition cap requested by the user. Fixed-level player normalization in the optional Circuit uses the same species ratio against that mode's stated baseline rather than incorrectly using the story cap. Original player parties are restored after the facility.
The Leveler, party-wide preparation, captures/gifts, received trades, Day Care, permanent evolutions/forms, storage withdrawals and battle entry must agree on the individual cap. Clamp newly owned over-cap Pokémon down, preserve their identity/build/held item/status and never revive a fainted Pokémon through normalization. Evolving/fusing can lower the cap; record and display the resulting level rather than blocking the evolution. Ordinary evolution's eligibility is checked on its pre-evolution species, including the existing at-cap convenience.
Preparation and summary displays show the selected Pokémon's actual individual cap. A party-wide completion message distinguishes the chapter cap from individual caps. The player must not discover the rule through unexplained stat loss or a generic “no effect” message. Full legendary teams remain selectable if otherwise legal.


MEGA CAP CLARIFICATION — USER CORRECTION
There is NO additional player level-cap penalty for Mega Evolution, matching Mega Stones, Dragon Ascent, or Primal Orbs. The proposed 95-percent Mega-ready rule was a misunderstanding and is withdrawn. The legendary BST cap above remains: a legendary Mega user retains only its ordinary legendary-species adjustment, never an extra Mega surcharge. Ordinary Mega-capable Pokémon keep the full chapter cap.
Players can Mega Evolve once per battle. The user permits deliberately authored trainer exceptions with more than one Mega, including possible Elite Four situations; this is design discretion, not a blanket opponent rule or an implemented engine change. Preserve current authored trainer permissions until any specific exception is designed and validated.

Opponent levels — initial tuning baseline

These are Normal-mode starting targets, to be playtested with the actual teams.

| Encounter role | Level relative to the current player cap |
|---|---|
| Ordinary trainers | −2 through 0 |
| Strong expedition trainers and rivals | 0 through +1 |
| Gym Leaders and major bosses | Mostly +1 or +2 |
| Selected boss ace | Occasionally +3 |

Easy shifts those teams down two levels; Hard shifts them up two. Their strategies remain intact. Challenge should come primarily from coordinated teams, lead/reserve choices, targeting and resource management, rather than routine ten- or twenty-level gaps.

Opening battles before preparation access need deliberately authored opening levels under the shared level policy. Near the League, the implementation must explicitly resolve the level-100 ceiling; it must not silently compensate with extra stat multipliers. The blueprint records that boundary as a tuning decision.

You set out to become Hoenn's Champion with two partners. Helping an employee in the woods draws you into the theft of Devon's equipment. The deliveries that follow introduce Steven and Stern, who become recurring companions rather than assignment dispensers. Across the journey, you discover that Magma and Aqua are combining modern instruments, ancient accounts and stolen artifacts to locate powers they believe they can control.

The added places show the consequences of those efforts and the history that the teams misunderstand. The player helps people and Pokémon, follows concrete leads, and gradually becomes someone Steven and the Gym Leaders trust when the situation worsens. The League journey continues throughout: your badges, stronger team and growing field access let you go farther and take on greater responsibility.

Magma and Aqua are responsible for particular thefts and disturbances, not for the existence of every legendary Pokémon. The ruins are records of Hoenn's past, not a newly invented universal machine requiring one legendary from every island. Mew, Deoxys and the Regis retain their own identities. Finding, observing or resolving an encounter can advance the story without ownership of that Pokémon.

The opening crystal mystery receives its conclusion after the weather crisis. The Champion challenge then closes the journey you originally set out to make. The ending recognizes what you have done across Hoenn, as well as the League victory.

CONTINUITY
All designated story encounters occur in the established order. Optional shopping, collection, breeding, soot, berry trades and passenger fights never become substitutes for a required story event. A Gym badge does not silently stand in for completing an earlier required scene.

Progress is communicated through events and characters: a destination becomes known, a transport service can depart, an obstacle is resolved, or a character has a reason to meet you next. Do not add a visible research checklist or repeated generic report counter. When a conversation is necessary, it should resolve something specific or organize the next action. Characters exchange information without forcing the player to carry every update back to Rustboro.

Use the existing character interaction nearest the next leg wherever possible. Ordinary return travel remains available; progression gates control the next consequential scene, not the player's ability to leave, heal or retrieve a needed party member. A blocked story interaction names the actual unfinished event and where to go.


SIX ACTS — THE STORY STRUCTURE
Act I, C01–C14: leave home with two partners, earn trust through the woods/tunnel rescues, and follow the first deliveries to Dewford's discovery. The player wants to become Champion; helping people brings the larger mystery into that journey.
Act II, C15–C26: the museum theft and inland pursuit expose the teams' search for power. Mt. Chimney's aftermath leads directly through the woodland rescue, Moltres's roost and desert safeguards. Each added area shows a consequence or clarifies the next lead.
Act III, C27–C36: Surf opens the east; New Mauville and the occupied Institute connect local anomalies to the sea. The survey, Fortree and Lilycove lead into one substantial offshore voyage, ending at Faraway Island and pointing toward the Orb keepers.
Act IV, C37–C45: the Orb and submarine thefts turn investigation into pursuit. Maxie's failure, Heatran, Aqua Hideout, the Space Center, Birth Island, the wreck and the ruins supply successive concrete leads while the acute simultaneous crisis has not yet begun.
Act V, C46–C48: Kyogre's awakening demands an immediate response. Prior discoveries ground the Sky Pillar solution. Once Sootopolis is safe, Juan and the crystal/origins conclusion close the remaining story thread without requiring legendary ownership.
Act VI, C49–C50: Wally and the League pay off the trainer journey. Becoming Champion ends a complete story; optional collection and exhibitions remain optional.

GUIDE-FREE NAVIGATION — REQUIRED PLAYER EXPERIENCE
The player must always know the next required destination and action without an external guide. Each chapter below owns an explicit handoff: named place, practical route/entrance, named person or object, and any required party capability/item. Atmospheric dialogue may precede it but cannot replace it. The handoff is mandatory before player control returns from a completed gated event.
Repeat the current direction when the relevant character is spoken to again. Reward-claimed and already-completed branches must not overwrite it with generic flavor. If that actor departs or a legendary disappears, its existing interaction point or the departure/harbor character retains the clue. An optional capture's success, failure or refusal must not swallow the main-story direction.
When several prerequisites are missing, state the NEXT unmet step in playable order, not an opaque list of flags. At a gate, explain both why the player cannot advance and exactly where to resolve it. Name the source of a missing field license, required move, transport permission or recoverable Castform. Never send the player to a location blocked by the very permission they are trying to earn.
Use the existing PokeNav region map for destination names, route numbers and supported markers. Imported locations must have working labels and directions from a known town or route. Existing entrances and actors are preferred; a new quest journal, global tracker or extra hint NPC is not required by this rule. Puzzle inscriptions must include plain-English actionable instructions; Braille knowledge and an external walkthrough are not progression requirements.
The 50 handoffs are authored text content. Implementers may split them into native text boxes and adjust terminology to match the real menu, but may not remove a destination, action, requirement or repeatable retrieval path. Exact map geometry and controller actions must be checked before shipping, especially the Route134 currents, deep-cave branches and Sky Pillar bike route. If a necessary fork is ambiguous, update the existing local interaction/landmark guidance and validate it from a fresh approach; do not claim that saying only a dungeon's name solves internal navigation.

ONE STORY AND ONE REQUIRED ORDER
The required story spine is C01 → first-arrival C03 access → C02 → C04 → C05 → C07 → C08 → C09 → C10 → C12 → C13 → C14 → C16 → C17 → C18 Wally → C19 → C20 reunion → C22 → C23 → C24 → C25 → C26 → C27 → C28 → C29 → C30 → C31 rival/Scope/Winona → C32 rival/harbor → C34 first voyage → C35 → C36 → C37 → C38 → C39 → C40 → C41 → C42 → C43 → C44 → C45 chamber and three ruins → C46 → C47 → C48 → C49 → C50.
C06, C11, C15, C21, C33 and optional services within other chapters are route/preparation opportunities, not requirements to spend, breed, harvest, collect or win optional fights. Required licenses and story interactions at those places remain explicitly named. Story scenes gate the next required event in this spine. Ordinary healing, return transport, preparation and access to already-open habitats remain available. Kartana's preserved access is not changed by this ordering.
Research is what characters sometimes do within this story; it is not a second progression track. Internal report/accomplishment identities may record persistence, but the player receives concrete dialogue and consequences. Generic report turn-ins do not become extra stages. Capturing a named legendary is optional unless an explicitly optional acquisition itself requires it.

C01 — A journey with two partners
Choose both starters and rescue Birch in the existing opening. Birch sees that you can coordinate a pair and encourages the journey. Preserve the rival's remaining-third-starter rule. Initial cap: 14.

Retained exact contract:
Starter identity contract: record generation, first selected starter and second selected starter independently. The rival uses the remaining third regional starter, as 7.1 GetEmeraldChampionsRivalStarterIndex does; character gender selects the presentation variant. Old TRAINER ID suffixes are not a reason to give the rival one of the player’s selected partners. Both starter ownership and Mega receipts stay separate.

PLAYER HANDOFF — Birch at the rescue/send-off interaction:
“Go north from Littleroot along Route 101 to Oldale. Heal and prepare at its Pokémon Center, then take the north exit to Route 103 and meet your rival.”
Repeat availability: the same existing interaction keeps the current direction until its destination event is completed; when it cannot remain, use the existing departure interaction as described in the navigation contract.

C03 — Oldale before the first real test
On the first visit, the Center gives practical access to preparation, healing, storage, the Leveler and catching supplies. Let the player try those services before continuing north. This stop supplies the tools for the game without making every tutorial mandatory.

C02 therefore includes the optional Oldale preparation stop before its rival sub-event.

C12 — Steven in Granite Cave

C13 — Brawly and Mega access
Defeat Brawly, then return to Steven in his Granite Cave room to complete the letter/badge/Ring handoff. Brawly explicitly repeats those directions after the battle. Brawly's coordination test and the Ring expand the player's practical options. Deliver the supported starter stone entitlements, preserving independent receipts and pending delivery. No unsupported starter receives an invented Mega. Preserve the original overlapping Lilith/Brenden approach as ordinary back-to-back trainer encounters. Brenden may challenge immediately after Lilith, creating first-pass endurance pressure, but each victory persists independently. Losing to Brenden leaves Lilith defeated; the player can heal, rearrange the team and return to Brenden alone. Do not impose a full reset merely because sight lines overlap. Separately announced, deliberately balanced endurance challenges may require a restart from their first fight.

C13 STARTER-MEGA ENTITLEMENTS — EXACT DESIGN OWNER
After the letter/Brawly/Ring conditions, process BOTH original starters independently using the recorded original selections, even if those Pokémon have since evolved, been boxed or left the party. The rival's leftover starter does not create a player entitlement.
For each listed stone: if unowned, deliver it or retain a pending delivery; if already owned through an earlier finite world source, award the standard one-time 3,000 duplicate-Mega payment and close this starter entitlement. A later world source uses its reciprocal finite duplicate rule. Never pay/give twice for the same starter-stone entitlement. Charizard has TWO independent stone entitlements, not a menu that permanently discards one.

C14 — The manor and the song
The manor investigation and meadow performance reveal the next part of the old account: earlier travelers saw related phenomena across the land and sea, and left a lead toward a crystal chamber beneath Sootopolis. The song/Meloetta discovery is something the player witnesses. Meloetta ownership is not a key. Steven's immediate conclusion is that Stern's observations may explain what has changed now. Finish the chapter and reach cap 24, then sail onward to Slateport.

WHAT EACH C45 SITE CONTRIBUTES
The Sealed Chamber’s inner account explains that its route record was preserved at the three named ruins. It opens those sites and gives their exact modern map names through the player’s interpretation. This is knowledge of geography and history, not a device powered by three captured Regis.
Desert Ruins supplies the first geographical constraint: the sought entrance lies in the eastern seabed south of the sky-watchers’ island. The player’s map identifies that island as Mossdeep. Its account also warns against disturbing the land power.
Island Cave supplies the second: the old approach begins under a deep-water basin rather than by following the surface currents into the western channels. This distinguishes the misleading echoes picked up by the Scanner. Its account warns that the sea power cannot be commanded by an artifact alone.
Ancient Tomb supplies the last route relationship: the basin leads into a submerged cave where the passage rises above the waterline. Combined with the Scanner region and the other two descriptions, this identifies the Route128 Seafloor Cavern approach. It also preserves the account of appealing to the sky guardian when land and sea clash.
At whichever site is completed last, the player-facing conclusion explicitly says: “The three accounts match the Scanner’s southeastern signal. From Mossdeep, sail south through Route127 to Route128. Dive at the deep-water basin, enter the underwater cave, and surface where you find the submarine. That is Aqua’s route.” The route/entrance must be shown and validated in the actual map presentation. The final prompt also reminds the player to bring licensed Surf/Dive and compatible Strength/Rock Smash access for the cavern. No extra return to Stern is needed to approve these already-understood findings.

3. ECONOMY — ONE PURPOSE FOR EACH REWARD
========================================

AUTHORITATIVE ITEM POLICY
- Centers: free healing, Leveler, legal moves/build editing, Nature/Ability/EV and useful-IV preparation; fixed maximum PP; ordinary competitive held equipment.
- Battle-set preparation goes straight from service selection to Pokémon selection, format and a set preview. Keep the final apply confirmation and special-item handling; do not repeat a multi-page explanation on every visit.
- Held combat effects and healing/revival moves remain part of battle. Naturally activated held berries, White Herb, Weakness Policy and similar equipment are legal. They remain consumed during the battle unless a native move/ability restores them. Champions battle settlement restores each player Pokémon’s battle-start held item, including berries; this is not permission to use manual medicine or X items.
- Potions, Revives, status medicine and Ether/Elixir remain purchasable OUTSIDE-BATTLE conveniences. They save a trip/refill during exploration; they cannot brute-force trainer fights. In wild battle, permit Balls but not manual medicine/X-item spending. Free Center recovery, one-charge refillable Vial and planned rest points prevent mandatory medicine purchases.
- Free battle berries/equipment are for equipping; do not allow unlimited free manual field medicine or resale through that service. Garden currency comes from harvesting/gifts, not free battle presets.
- X-items, PP Up/PP Max, EXP-only items, Hyper Training/Bottle Cap services and redundant paid move-teaching are retired. Restoring CURRENT PP is different from increasing maximum PP.
- Evolution purchases acquire a new species/form, rather than charge for stat/move editing. Stones 3,000; ordinary evolution tools 5,000; reusable devices 10,000, once. Evolution/progression items are explicit exceptions to the free ORDINARY held-gear catalogue; their incidental held effects do not allow a preset to manufacture them.
- Free form tools remain free when their form-access condition is satisfied. Mega Stones are earned world rewards, never a free global archive.
- Key/Mega/reusable progression items cannot be sold or discarded. NPC trades return their held item before exchanging the Pokémon. Free gear has sale value zero. Balls have sale value zero so the basic restock cannot generate money.
- Basic Balls: Centers replenish ordinary Poké Balls up to 10 if below 10, free. This is a safety net, not an unlimited saleable stock. Bulk/specialized Balls remain convenient purchases.
- Planned purchase prices: Poké Ball 100, Great Ball 300, Ultra Ball 600; ordinary specialist Balls 600; Luxury/Premier-style cosmetic preferences may cost more but have no required combat advantage. Dream/Beast specialty access remains optional.
- Medicine starting prices: Potion 200, Super Potion 700, Hyper Potion 1,500; Revive 2,000; Full Heal 600; Ether 1,000. Late medicine/PP stocks retain local progression; exact unlisted values are seed values pending budget testing, not an invitation to invent prices in dialogue.
- Retry restores the battle checkpoint, including borrowed held-item state, with no cash penalty or duplicate reward. Ordinary defeat also cannot permanently exhaust the ability to continue. Field consumables used before the checkpoint remain spent.
- Reward claim, successful delivery and completed story event are different. Full storage preserves a pending reward, not a repeated fight or lost entitlement.

WHY TWO SOURCES CAN STILL MAKE SENSE
A merchant offers certainty and early choice; an exploration gift saves a purchase. A consumable can usefully repeat. A reusable tool or one-per-owner Mega must not become a useless repeat:
* A one-time reusable-device gift checks Bag/PC/held ownership and its own receipt. If already owned, offer a clearly named 5,000 treasure/cash alternative once. The early purchase bought earlier access; later exploration still pays.
* Finite duplicate Mega world entitlements become a one-time 3,000 research payment when that stone is already owned. Never reopen a claim on re-entry. This is an explicit proposed change to the old duplicate-source design.
* A shop refuses to sell a redundant reusable key device. An alternate BP purchase does not evade ownership checks.
* Repeatable freebies cannot turn into repeatable sellable gifts through any substitute rule. Substitutions apply only to finite authored entitlements.

SOOT: EXPLORATION MILESTONES, NOT A SECOND SHOPPING BALANCE
Keep existing ash paths and Sack. Count lifetime collection; no spending reduces progress.
100: Linking Cord if missing, otherwise the one-time 5,000 alternative.
250: unlock the Marshadow discovery; it does NOT count as a capture.
500: Houndoominite or the finite duplicate-Mega alternative.
Retire the separate soot purchasing balance and the redundant encounter/status-flute rewards. Existing glassmaker actors explain progress and sell decorative glass furniture for ordinary money. No new counter or map prop is required. Chairs/desks are optional cosmetic purchases (initial 6,000/8,000 cash). Repeated walks can earn the milestones, but none is required for the campaign or a basic evolution.

GARDEN BERRIES: A DISTINCT OPTIONAL EXPLORATION CURRENCY
Keep all eleven existing eligible berries: Razz, Bluk, Nanab, Wepear, Pinap, Pomeg, Kelpsy, Qualot, Hondew, Grepa, Tamato.
Each of Baxcalibrite, Dragoninite and Tyranitarite costs 20 total eligible berries in any mixture, once. No battle-berry substitution, free-preset source, invisible species sacrifice or mandatory planting wait.
Preserve existing garden locations and harvest identities. The book does not assert that 60 berries are already available on the mandatory route before the first trade; measure legitimate harvest/gift supply before accepting the price. A dedicated optional gardener can obtain stones earlier, while ordinary collection over the campaign provides an alternative. Do NOT add automatic chapter gifts of 60 berries merely to make the accounting pass.
The trade UI and NPC name the eligible currency, cost, current count, chosen stone and already-claimed state. Charge only on successful delivery.
If a future alternate source makes a traded stone already owned, this trade becomes unavailable without spending berries; do not charge 20 berries for the 3,000 duplicate cash substitution.

SHOAL CAVE
Keep four Shoal Salt + four Shoal Shell for the first Glalitite. Later collections give a Big Pearl. If Glalitite is already owned before this finite first claim, the first claim also gives a Big Pearl and closes the unique entitlement. No second Linking Cord reward. Real-time tides and repeated material collection remain OPTIONAL; no campaign gate waits for a tide or a harvest.

SHARDS
Keep colored shard → corresponding evolution stone as a cash-saving alternative through the existing Route124 treasure hunter. Stones are consumable, so repeat exchanges can be useful for another family member. No free source of shards through battle preparation. The exchange states the output before charging.

COINS
Keep direct Coin purchases at 20 cash per Coin; no required gambling. Ordinary starter alternatives: 500 Coins = 10,000 cash, one finite entitlement per offered species, respecting original starter receipts. Poipole 6,500 and Genesect 7,500 Coins remain seed prices (130,000/150,000 cash), marked for optional-collection affordability testing. They are not mandatory campaign gates and are not claimed affordable on first arrival. Do not replace a meaningful existing Pokémon gift with a redundant purchased copy.

BP
Circuit BP is optional mastery income. Remove paid shelves of free gear and retired PP upgrades/X-items. Stock specialty Balls, selected field recovery, cosmetics and paid evolution alternatives. Working values: regular special Balls 2 BP; Dream/Beast 8; ordinary evolution tools 8–16; reusable Cord 8 with the same ownership check. BP-earned items may retain ordinary resale only where the item is normally saleable; cash buying and selling must never be profitable. This is earned income, not a free-stock loop. No basic move, stat or Ability choice requires BP.

FOSSILS, GIFTS AND TRADES
Fossil acquisition is the exploration reward; revival is free and quick. Keep the existing one-time gifts/trades and their local identity unless a named row changes them. Do not require another emulator for evolution. Linking Cord is reusable; Metal Coat, King's Rock and similar item evolutions work by local item use. Additional location/party conditions must be stated before item consumption. No gift-only baby requirement is introduced by this revision.

DYNAMIC OFFERS
An NPC never promises a reward before checking eligibility/receipt. Dialogue uses the actual item/cost and a useful already-owned alternative. Conditional trainer-side Pokémon do not create new permissions for player presets. A retired item cannot remain in a shop description, prize menu, Pickup result or gift message.


4. FUNDING AND DUPLICATION CHECKS — FIRST NUMERICAL BUDGET
==========================================================

This is a PROPOSED guaranteed funding floor, not a measured 7.1 playthrough. Amounts below are one-time supplemental story stipends INCLUDING the opening cash. Trainer prize money, optional loot and activity income are additional and are not counted twice as stipends.

Start 6,000; C07 +3,000; C09 +4,000; C16 +8,000; C19 +4,000; C22 +6,000; C26 +8,000; C27 +5,000; C28 +6,000; C30 +6,000; C31 +8,000; C36 +12,000; C39 +10,000; C40 +10,000; C42 +12,000; C43 +12,000; C44 +12,000; C45 +16,000; C46 +16,000; C47 +14,000; C48 +20,000; C50 +25,000.

Milestone transaction: completing the event earns the stipend once; reporting it later cannot re-earn it. A battle prize and a separate stipend may both exist, but each has one owner and appears in the budget. Do not scale the stipend with difficulty, opponent level or number of battle variants.

Early check before Roxanne: 6,000 buys one 3,000 stone and 20 ordinary Poké Balls at 100 each, with 1,000 left; free preparation/healing/basic Balls remain available. After C16 the stipend floor is 21,000, before trainer prizes. That can fund a 10,000 Cord, three 3,000 stones and a small reserve; it does not promise every optional purchase simultaneously.
At each later milestone, test at least a replacement team with several paid evolutions plus capture supplies. Expensive collectible Pokémon can remain savings goals. If the retained-trainer cut reduces normal income below those practical needs, adjust guaranteed stipends or prices, not a mandatory grinding loop.
Never use old last-party-member levels to derive the new prize economy. First-clear prize mapping: regular/casual/grunt = 20×; ace/gym/rival/brain = 40×; leader/admin/boss and non-League elite exhibitions = 100×; E0493–E0496 Elite Four = 150×; E0497 Champion explicitly = 200×. Multiply by the INCOMING live player cap snapshotted before battle and before any milestone increase. Pay once per actual fight receipt, never per owner/variant/member. No difficulty multiplier. E0409 pays once. A grouping label does not create or merge a reward receipt. Replays and rewards need explicit renewal rules. No new endlessly rewarding practice rematch is silently added here.


5. FIFTY ABILITIES AND THE DOUBLES CURRICULUM — DESIGN
======================================================

This is a curated first library, not a claim that these are objectively the fifty best abilities or every cool strategy. The first 24 are pivotal abilities; weather pairs coalesce into fewer complete team concepts. The remaining 26 support those concepts or make distinct answers/finishers. Other useful mechanics (Misty Surge, Ruin abilities, Dry Skin, Queenly Majesty, Mold Breaker, Technician, Adaptability, etc.) remain available; absence from this first fifty is not a species/ability ban.

Availability is the merged, resolved National Dex + genuine Inclement/Champions additions catalogue. A trainer assignment does not create an ability permission. A literal seed-carrier list is only presence, not proof of a useful lead or native execution. Mega abilities need the transformation to actually happen. Every proposed engine must be demonstrated in the native rules without Dynamax/Tera assumptions.

For each engine record: primary pair, alternate lead, actual move/ability/item/EVs, relative speed, survival after any ally hit, first two useful turns, fallback if disrupted, reserve contribution and counterplay. New teams do not require a new overworld actor. Prefer a retained encounter whose region/character suits it.

6. BOSS IDENTITIES AND CONCRETE SEED REPAIRS
============================================

These cards preserve the good 7.1 identities while defining what must improve. They do not pretend that every seed moveset is already final. A named BLOCKER must be resolved in this book before the affected scene/team is accepted. Existing overworld encounters are reused; a roster revision does not authorize moving the actor.

No unsupported combo counts as coverage. Difficulty should come from competent alternative lines, not a fragile script that only works when the player cooperates. Field and battle evidence are different: headless scene completion cannot establish competitive decision quality.

E0030 Roxanne
  Identity: Slow Rock pressure: Carbink Trick Room/Helping Hand, recoil-free Relicanth/Sudowoodo pressure, Nosepass Wide Guard.
  Review/repair: Her team must do useful things when Trick Room is denied; no pre-Ring Mega.

E0040 Brawly
  Identity: Redirection, positioning and physical finishers; Pachirisu supports genuine threats and Hawlucha has a real White Herb/Unburden line.
  Review/repair: Do not count special Cobalion as a Justified sweep. Preserve its Coaching/Quick Guard role unless deliberately reauthored.

E0052 Archie at Slateport
  Identity: Manual rain is a readable preview of Aqua’s later automatic weather teams.
  Review/repair: Wingull must choose weather versus immediate action sensibly; a disrupted setter cannot make all reserves dead weight.

E0092 Wattson
  Identity: Discharge + Motor Drive opening, terrain, and base-Manectric versus Mega timing.
  Review/repair: Do not block Electivire’s intended trigger with a misdirected single-target move; confirm custom Electrode Electric Surge permission.

E0131 Tabitha at Mt. Chimney
  Identity: Reactive Steam Engine pressure alongside independent Steel/Fire actions. Damaging Fire/Water hits can activate the ability; the Coalossal/Klang opening does not claim an authored allied trigger. E0337 owns the deliberate advanced self-activation lesson.
  Review/repair: DRAFT CHANGE: Weezing now has Levitate. Steam Engine remains active. Verify the actual trigger and survival; it is not a free boost on the team sheet.

E0132 Maxie at Mt. Chimney
  Identity: Sun + Tailwind/Chlorophyll, with Mega Camerupt used at a sensible time.
  Review/repair: Keep a useful line if sun is overwritten; do not portray possession of the specific legendary he is still trying to awaken.

E0150 Flannery
  Identity: After You Lilligant + Torkoal Eruption, with pivots and a different Mega reserve line.
  Review/repair: After You requires sun/speed/order and surviving Torkoal HP; the AI should not repeat it when Torkoal already moved or would do better independently.

E0171 Norman
  Identity: Weezing/Slaking suppression first; psychic/Download reserve mode after Gas exits or when suppression is deliberately accepted.
  Review/repair: DRAFT CHANGE: Weezing/Slaking lead the suppression mode. The psychic/Download/Mega reserves are a separate mode after Gas exits; do not assume their entry abilities work while it remains.

E0248 Shelly at the Institute
  Identity: Snow + Veil and Competitive pressure, contrasting Aqua’s usual rain.
  Review/repair: Kingdra is not a Swift Swim payoff here. Preserve that intentional coverage role or replace it coherently, not by silently changing weather.

E0289 Winona
  Identity: Tailwind, Contrary Enamorus and a late defensive Mega reserve.
  Review/repair: Each member needs a usable line when speed control is denied. Do not put every Flying attacker on the same three attacks.

E0320 Matt at Mt. Pyre
  Identity: Rain + Dry Skin/Swift Swim with an actual spread-defense decision.
  Review/repair: Heliolisk and Toxicroak should exploit their recovery/immunity roles; account for Grass and opposing weather.

E0337 Tabitha in Magma Hideout
  Identity: Dragapult weak Surf activates Steam Engine/Weakness Policy Coalossal; Volcanion offers a Water-absorption alternative.
  Review/repair: Critical native benchmark: survival of allied Surf plus likely enemy pressure without Dynamax/Tera. Minimal SpA on the physical trigger user; skip self-activation when weather or threats make it losing.

E0338 Courtney in Magma Hideout
  Identity: Sun-enhanced special pressure plus physical Protosynthesis contrast.
  Review/repair: Beads of Ruin can expose the ally’s SpD too. Do not treat an offensive aura as a free team-wide defense.

E0339 Maxie in Magma Hideout
  Identity: Sun/ground pressure as a culmination of Magma’s earlier tactics.
  Review/repair: DRAFT CHANGE: Torkoal/Drought replaces pre-awakening Groudon, retaining sun while fixing the chronology.

E0348 Matt in Aqua Hideout
  Identity: Rain + Swift Swim and Stamina Archaludon; screen support offers a different lead.
  Review/repair: Track both opponents, not just the rain damage boost. Avoid giving every reserve the same Water-only answer.

E0400 Tate and Liza
  Identity: Psychic Terrain plus a real Trick Room mode, with Mega Gardevoir as the powered payoff.
  Review/repair: Grounded terrain conditions, setter redundancy, Wide Guard and Dark matchups all matter. This is not six interchangeable Psychics.

E0408 Tabitha at Mossdeep

E0496 Drake
  Identity: Dragon offense with speed control and a credible alternative to linear setup.
  Review/repair: Mega Garchomp’s seed has no sand setter. Either it is a non-sand role with justified opportunity cost or the team must be revised; do not claim Sand Force synergy.

E0497 Wallace
  Identity: A championship balance test: rain, terrain, anti-Intimidate response and useful pivots.

E0512 Steven

7. DRAFT TEAM AMENDMENTS AND ACCEPTANCE
=======================================

The following earlier design amendments remain part of the v4 build library unless superseded by its current U/T records. The later trainer audit and single-review corrections are also integrated. Neither these textual edits nor the inherited 7.0 observations certify all 342 current fights at the new caps. Full move-pool, speed/survival and native multi-turn acceptance remain required. The global cap/level rule overrides old seed offsets. Changed prototype tactical hints must be reconciled with their new actors/actions; no stale hint may refer to a removed partner.

- E0131: Galarian Weezing uses Levitate in this draft, preserving Coalossal’s Steam Engine. Neutralizing Gas is not credited here.
- E0171: replace Bewear with Galarian Weezing; lead Weezing/Slaking. Slaking replaces recharge Giga Impact with Ice Punch and keeps Double-Edge. Psychic/Download/Mega reserve mode is entered after Gas leaves or when its suppression is acceptable. Six members, no new actor; native ordering/AI acceptance pending.
- E0339: Torkoal/Drought replaces Groudon. Maxie has a sun engine but does not already own the specific legendary he is trying to awaken.
- E0409: Maxie’s Rhyperior replaces Groudon; Courtney’s Ninetales supplies the opposing side’s sun. Combined roster stays three per opposing owner. Main-story Primal ownership is not invented.
- E0458: Pelipper/Drizzle replaces Kyogre. Archie’s team culminates the rain plan; the subsequent Kyogre awakening remains a separate field event. Primal battles belong to their later designated legendary scenes/exhibitions, not a contradictory pre-awakening party.
- E0076 Aisha variant: Froslass/Tauros leads a guaranteed-critical-hit Anger Point prototype, with Hariyama/Hitmontop reserves. The separately triggered single-owner format preserves the intended first pair; no claim of runtime proof.
- E0113: Ribombee/Oricorio lead an explicit Quiver Dance + Dancer prototype, with a second dance-capable reserve. Native copy ordering, no recursive-copy loop and useful alternative attacks require proof.
- E0199: Jani develops Simple + Costar. Clefairy supports Bibarel Swords Dance, then a deliberate support-slot switch admits Flamigo to copy existing Attack boosts. Rain is an alternate pressure mode, not a prerequisite for Costar.
- E0354: the retained sea pair becomes an expert Commander showcase. Dondozo/Tatsugiri occupy both slots; Rillaboom/Cresselia are a separate fallback mode. No impossible Flamigo switch into two occupied Commander slots. Dondozo uses Heavy Slam, avoiding a Grassy-Terrain-weakened Earthquake claim.
- E0475: Everett’s existing Trick House encounter becomes the explicit Perish/Shadow Tag prototype. Lapras supplies Perish Song, Wobbuffet supplies the trap, and the AI must release/switch its own threatened partners before their countdown expires. Ghost/escape-item counterplay remains.
- E0495: Alolan Sandslash replaces Walrein as the actual Slush Rush reserve. Snow/Veil and a distinct physical speed lane are now explicit; native benchmarks pending.
- E0506: Weak Armor prototype leads low-investment Ice Shard Weavile with Armarouge. A resisted PHYSICAL ally hit boosts Speed without pretending to activate Weakness Policy. Genesect/Mega Scolipede retain alternate pressure. Ally damage/redirect/AI proof pending.

No boss is deleted. Removing a legendary from a chronologically impossible early villain party does not remove its player discovery or later showcase. Groudon/Kyogre’s own designated legendary battles remain meaningful representation. No new overworld actor is needed for these team amendments.

DESIGN TEAM ACCEPTANCE
- One main plan, a useful alternate lead and a fallback when disrupted.
- Every active partner contributes; do not protect a harmless slot while its partner is removed.
- Ally hit targets, amount, hit category, immunity, stat stage and action order are explicit.
- No Dynamax/Tera-dependent plan in a Mega-focused ruleset.
- Each owner uses at most the supported Mega allowance; base-form abilities can justify delaying Mega.
- Repeated Protect is chosen for a concrete payoff, not a default loop.
- Legendary difficulty is strategic; no mandatory capture RNG or paid bag healing decides campaign progress.
- Important matchups get native multi-turn evidence. Source/roster scans establish candidates, not competent AI.


8. RETAINED TRAINERS AND THE CUT LEDGER
=======================================

EXISTING EXECUTABLE INTENT
The per-party existing-intent rows below preserve the actual current strategy preferences, trainer traits and explicit partnership candidates alongside the new tactical cards. These are conditional inputs to the shared paired evaluator, not fixed first-turn commands. A preference cannot bypass move legality, native order, HP costs, suppression, redirection, a better immediate result or the committed-player-input policy. Species-named partnerships follow the named Pokémon after an authored reorder. Reconcile a stale preference in this same book when its v4 team changes; do not discard all 7.0 tuning or pretend the prose cards automatically execute in the ROM.

BATTLE COUNT OWNER
The current v4 candidate has 342 distinct authored campaign trainer battles: 369 party definitions minus 25 mutually exclusive rival aliases, minus one duplicate owner definition for the Meteor Falls multi battle, minus one for the Space Center multi battle. The 324 active E groups are authoring groupings, not the number of actual fights. Separate trainers grouped together remain separate fights; actual two-owner battles count once. The target is 300–350 such campaign trainer encounters, required and optional combined. Random wild battles, optional legendary capture attempts, Retry attempts, repeat interviews/rematches and endless facility/Circuit runs are reported separately and never used to inflate or satisfy that finite trainer target. Scripted capture-capable story encounters and the opening rescue remain explicitly listed in the story, not hidden additional trainer records.
The required subset is determined by the story spine, its named bosses/guards and the actual route geometry, not by calling all 342 battles mandatory. The five ship passenger fights, Winstrate challenge and named exhibitions remain optional. Traversal must reconcile required/avoidable sight lines; a metadata label alone is not proof of avoidability. The user permits further justified cuts/additions, so 342 is the reviewed implementation baseline rather than a promise that this count is already ideally paced.


Retained party ORDER and U build IDs are explicit. Each U(+n) now gives the exact member offset from the incoming live player cap on Medium/Normal; apply Easy −2 or Hard +2 and clamp 1–100. The first two listed members lead in ordinary single-owner doubles. For multi battles, one member per owner leads; see the formation contracts below. T references contain the complete supplied tactical plan in section 22. Alternate deployment is a tactical fixture, not authorization for an unimplemented automatic lead reorder. E groups are inherited authoring units: some contain starter/gender variants, two owners or dynamic native pairs. They are not all literally one fight on every route. The isolated implementation reconciled 140 retired groups to 142 trainer identities and 151 map battle entry sites; their actors retain civilian dialogue. This does not measure the number of fights on one played route. That first 140-group pass is historical; the current count and five additional v4 removals are owned above. No exact unavoidable-playthrough percentage is claimed.

Cut design: remove the battle requirement and preserve useful dialogue/gifts at the existing actor. Remove a purposeless actor only after dependency/spatial review. Do not leave battle-only flags guarding a retained reward. Protected encounters and valuable strategies are checked separately.

C42 STEVEN ALLY CONTRACT
Party U1501,U1502,U1503 in that order, level = incoming player cap (72 on the proposed first visit), not the opponent difficulty offset. IV defaults above. Species/items/moves/natures reuse PARTNER_STEVEN, not E0512. The explicit EV spreads are proposed normalized modern spreads; the old partner file's legacy 2/32-style investments are not silently treated as complete 510-EV builds.
Each owner has at most one eligible Mega. Steven carries no Mega Stone and has no eligible Mega in this fixed party; player allowance is not transferred to him. Maxie/Courtney each retain their own one-Mega limit. The temporary three-member selection never permanently overwrites the player's other Pokémon.


10. PLACE-BY-PLACE ECONOMY DISPOSITIONS
=======================================

These rows are the actionable replacement ledger for existing locations. They do not move coordinates or create new props.
RULES:
KEEP = keep its 7.1 item/service purpose subject to the global price/receipt policy.
MOVE LESSON / TM = free move access already exists: a field TM pickup becomes a 1,500 research/treasure payment; an NPC teaching a redundant move becomes a concise strategy coach, without charging for the move.
EXP-only gift/pickup = 10 Great Balls. PP Up/PP Max = Ether/Max Ether respectively, outside battle. Vitamins = 5 Great Balls. Bottle Cap/Gold Bottle Cap = 3,000/10,000 treasure.
FREE HELD GEAR at a finite field/NPC reward = a local 10-Ball pack (Net on water/coast; Dusk in caves; Quick on ordinary land). The Center already supplies the gear. A clearly identified family-specific teaching gift may remain a demonstration, but it is not sold as a valuable economic prize.
Garden berries stay garden resources. Free battle berries are held-only preparation; an old renewable source cannot become renewable sellable cash by substitution.
Already-owned reusable/Mega substitutions apply only to FINITE entitlements. Native variable rewards are listed by their shared contract; no unresolved dynamic value is silently guessed.
The changed item/message/receipt and any dependent dialogue must be changed together later. The code is untouched now.

10C. NATIVE/SPECIAL OFFERS AND GIFTS
====================================

Centers: free ordinary gear and preparation, field tools and basic Ball restock. Progression/evolution tools are not conjured by free sets.
Rustboro specialist: Fire/Water/Thunder/Leaf/Moon/Sun Stones before Roxanne, 3,000 each.
Slateport specialist: all ten ordinary stones; Cord, Metal Coat, King's Rock, Dragon Scale, Deep Sea Tooth/Scale; prices 3,000/5,000/10,000 by item class.
Lilycove 4F: full ordinary evolution collection; no redundant move-service charge. 2F ordinary recovery/Balls; 3F advanced Balls and field recovery; 5F decorations; roof drinks/clearance. Drinks are optional field recovery, not battle power.
Route113 glassmaker: lifetime soot milestones only; furniture for cash. Retired flute/status/encounter-rate wares are not sold as necessary conveniences.
Berry Master: three 20-berry trades and existing ordinary garden gifts; one owner per stone claim.
Route124 treasure hunter: shard-to-stone offers, stated before charge.
Shoal keeper: first Glalitite, then Big Pearl; no Cord duplication.
Fallarbor Heart Scale trader: retire the PP Up exchange. A Heart Scale becomes ordinary collectible treasure sold for 1,000; this NPC gives free preparation advice rather than a redundant second currency loop.
Slateport market: cash field herb/PP supplies, optional decorations; no link-only Berry Powder requirement.
Game Corner: 27 starter-species entitlements plus Poipole/Genesect, with stated Coin prices and direct Coin purchase.
Circuit/Frontier desks: the shared Circuit, its BP stock and finite legendary milestones; do not resurrect every dormant native facility as an extra compulsory campaign.
Fossils: existing Devon revival, free. Keep every fossil the world actually supplies supported by the revival service.
Original starters: two permanent partners; supported original-starter Mega entitlements supplied by Steven after letter + Brawly/Ring.
Gift eggs: Togepi/Day Care and Wynaut/Lavaridge; no mandatory egg-hatching gate. Genuine Day Care breeding + hatch keeps its separate Kangaskhanite entitlement; a gift egg does not satisfy it.
Indeedee-F/Wanda's house and Cosplay Pikachu/Contest services remain optional. Later research partners use their own conditions; no retroactive claim that every special form is a pre-League gift.
Beldum: DESIGN moves Steven's gift to the Space Center chapter, with a prepared, cap-safe partner. Castform remains the guaranteed Institute gift needed by the survey.
Trades: Zigzagoon→Fidough (Rustboro); Croagunk→Tropius (Dewford); Igglybuff→Chansey (Verdanturf, despite old HAPPINY ID); Volbeat→Bombirdier (Fortree); Bagon→Cyclizar (Pacifidlog); Skitty→Type: Null (Frontier). Optional, confirm exact requested species and return held gear before completion.
Arceus/Magearna and other legendary gifts: retain source eligibility provisionally unless a specific campaign record changes it. Magearna's Diancie condition gates that acquisition, not the mandatory research report. Arceus is not automatically a reward for completing the entire curated Pokédex.

VARIABLE ITEM PROVIDERS — EXPLICIT TRANSACTIONS
These bindings resolve the old variable-item placeholders. Shared delivery, pending storage and no-duplicate rules still apply.
M036 Route120 Berry Beauty: one daily Figy/Wiki/Mago/Aguav/Iapapa Berry. The player trainer ID’s last digit chooses Figy for 0/5, Wiki 1/6, Mago 2/7, Aguav 3/8, Iapapa 4/9. Set the daily receipt only after successful delivery; full storage permits retry. These are not eligible garden-trade currency berries.
M177 Lilycove lottery: one optional draw per day, using the native party/PC OT-number match. Two matching trailing digits earn one Ether; three earn one Linking Cord if missing; four earn one Max Ether; five earn one Master Ball. A three-digit Cord prize when already owned instead earns ten Ultra Balls, with zero resale, not repeatable cash or another useless reusable key. This is the only added substitution here. The draw is consumed once, and an undelivered prize remains pending before any new draw. Pending delivery and its actual quantity survive a full Bag and date change; re-entry cannot redraw or duplicate it. If a pending Cord becomes redundant before delivery, resolve that same entitlement to the ten-Ball alternative. Implement the quantity-aware pending case and test it; it is not claimed present in the partial source.
M177 GivePrizeFromEarlier: delivers that exact pending lottery entitlement, then clears it only on success. It is not a second prize source and does not reset the daily draw receipt.
M513 Glass Workshop GiveGlassFlute: retired by the soot redesign. No variable flute reward remains; use the explicit lifetime milestones and cash-priced furniture already specified.
M518 Route124 diving treasure hunter: trade one Red Shard for one Fire Stone, Yellow for Thunder, Blue for Water, Green for Leaf. Preview the exact output and consume the shard only when delivery can succeed, including the existing case where consuming the final shard frees its inventory slot. Full storage/decline preserves the shard. Repeat exchanges are allowed because the stones are consumed by evolution; no free-preset shard source is added.

12. WILD DISTRIBUTION — PRESERVE THE 7.1 TEMPLATE
=================================================

These are the existing source species/methods/probabilities, not a new redistribution. Map IDs resolve in the index at the end. Keep habitat identity and sensible early options; evaluate whole families before changing any table. Do not lower ordinary encounter rates to create a new grind. Feebas and explicit legendary rules remain separately identified exceptions.

Ordinary encounter level uses its source range capped to the live player cap; the free Leveler makes a lower-level capture usable immediately. Named legendary encounter levels may be live cap plus a defined offset, with owned acquisition normalized down afterward. The seed table level is not evidence of earliest physical access.



All registered Hoenn method tables. Repeated map rows can represent time or other alternatives; those activations are not collapsed into one false probability. Percentages are conditional table weights, not the chance per walking step. Legendary injection, Sweet Scent and special encounters can change the outcome.

13. EVOLUTION RELATIONSHIPS — TEMPLATE WITH APPROVED NO-REPETITION OVERRIDES


NO-REPETITION EVOLUTION POLICY — APPROVED DIRECTION
Remove the twenty-use, thousand-step, cumulative-recoil and three-critical-hit chores in the eight amended rows below. Use the existing free Leveler/evolution confirmation, including at the current cap. Honor decline/Everstone behavior. No new training NPC, evolution currency or extra tutorial battle is added.
Keep meaningful known-move, exact-form/gender, location, party, item and existing explicit level requirements. Do not invent a new level threshold for a counter rule whose seed floor was zero: deleting the grind does not justify silently delaying access. Earlier practical use of these evolutions is an intentional convenience; evaluate any actual balance consequence through the normal roster/battle process, not an automatic counter reinstatement.
Friendship retains the existing free bonding service. Leek remains useful battle equipment rather than an evolution-counter tax. These are the intended evolution rules. Their scoped implementation evidence does not replace final source-bound release verification.
=============================================

The actual preprocessed source methods and additional conditions are preserved. This is not the full form-change or move-permission catalogue. Species/level/location/party conditions remain explicit.

15. POKÉMON SHOWCASE WATCHLIST — CURATION SEED
==============================================

The current reference watchlist is preserved below, including its gaps. The retained/draft trainer library is the real roster for this revision; this older signal list is a SEED CHECK, not a second final team owner. New draft teams in section 7 can close some gaps and remove other literal appearances. Dedicated legendary battles count as memorable encounters, not automatically trainer showcases. Final accepted family curation remains open.


This is an initial editorial selection, not an objective ranking or a user-approved final roster. It includes all starter finals, classic favorites, modern standouts, distinctive doubles supports, every item-Mega base and the registered legendary families. The pinned source retains the broader configured roster; this shortened book does not contain a separate exhaustive species index. Exact regional/form identities stay separate except true source enum aliases.

Missing retained authored showcases: ARBOLIVA, ARTICUNO_GALAR, DECIDUEYE_HISUI, DEOXYS_NORMAL, FLUTTER_MANE, GHOLDENGO, GLASTRIER, HO_OH, HYDRAPPLE, IRON_BUNDLE, IRON_HANDS, IRON_VALIANT, JIRACHI, KINGAMBIT, LILLIGANT_HISUI, LUGIA, MAGEARNA_ORIGINAL, MARACTUS, MEOWSCARADA, MEW, MOLTRES, MOLTRES_GALAR, PALAFIN_HERO, PECHARUNT, RAGING_BOLT, REGICE, REGIGIGAS, REGIROCK, REGISTEEL, ROARING_MOON, TATSUGIRI_DROOPY, TATSUGIRI_STRETCHY, TINKATON, TOEDSCRUEL, WALKING_WAKE, ZAPDOS_GALAR, ZOROARK, ZYGARDE. 16. MAP INDEX AND OVERWORLD ACCEPTANCE
======================================

Map IDs used elsewhere resolve here. These are registered Hoenn source maps, including dormant/support/facility layouts. Registration is not proof of campaign access. The redesigned campaign uses existing geography; unused imports do not become compulsory just because they appear in the index.

Selected exploration landmarks must have a named, geographically sensible region-map marker in the existing icon style. Specify reveal-on-briefing versus reveal-on-visit; do not equate a MAPSEC constant with a visibly correct icon or a Fly destination. Ember Path, Ashen Woods, Seaspray Cave, Sandstrewn Ruins and Dewford Manor already have source landmark identities. Their marker appearance and position still need screenshots.

Reuse original Emerald/Inclement hand-authored actors, pickup locations and paths. Our later additions are not original placements and do not gain visual approval merely because a current source inventory calls them existing or KEEP. Prefer replacing an obsolete original pickup at its authored position with the desired reward and appropriate native icon, after checking its original provenance, chapter, family access, collision/elevation, approach visibility, receipt and dependent dialogue. Review the room composition and narrative purpose as well: a valid floor tile is not sufficient, and a legendary chamber must retain its intended focal point. Do not invent coordinates, scatter sparkles, or convert every old item indiscriminately. New props, actors and effects must have a clear purpose and receive visual review. A retained trainer becoming a civilian is preferable to removing useful local information.

USER CORRECTION — DIANCIE CHAMBER: the later-added Diancite sparkle at (7,9) is rejected and must be removed. Relocate its existing finite reward to the original ShoalCave_LowTideStairsRoom visible pickup at (13,12,z3), replacing the dispensable Ice Heal; do not delete the entitlement or invent another chamber coordinate. No additional observation sparkle is needed. Keep the original central Diancie presentation. The later-added Wallace staging also requires visual review; its current inventory entry is not acceptance. The M287/M522 reward inventory records this replacement; its rendered composition still requires user visual review. Also delete the old M242 Beast Ball pickup because the later-added Jirachi door behind it made optional collection mandatory. Preserve the existing doorway and floor.

LATER-ADDED ACTOR REVIEW: the current meadow warden at (27,12), manor historian at (14,10), Sandstrewn archaeologist at (5,14), elevated-ruins researcher at (15,12), and Diancie-chamber Wallace at (11,10) are our later additions when compared with original Inclement history. Their story roles and their physical staging are separate questions; the present coordinates are not visual acceptance. Review normal approaches and room composition before retaining or changing those placements. Ember Path's unbound Warden script is not evidence of an existing actor and is not a reason to create another NPC.

For every NEW or materially restaged scene: headless simulation + useful screenshots + USER VISUAL REVIEW before acceptance. Record source/ROM identity, story state, approach route, actor start/end positions, camera, dialogue, movements, effects, battle outcome, rewards, control release and re-entry. No scene in this document has that acceptance yet.
