17. OVERWORLD SEQUENCES, DIALOGUE AND GUIDE-FREE PRESENTATION
================================================================

The story and its mandatory player handoffs are authored in section 2. This section owns the scene presentation, additional dialogue and local puzzle guidance. New or materially restaged scenes remain subject to rendered screenshots and user review. Current prose is the v4 implementation target, not a claim of completed visual acceptance.

These are part of the intended game. Existing geography, established actors and supported effects are the starting point. Dialogue, scene logic and a rendered review are needed even when no new sprite sheet is needed.

1. Dewford discovery: connect the manor account and meadow song through the historian/warden interactions and Steven's established conversation. The current historian and warden are later-added actors; their physical placement is not accepted merely because they exist in the checkout. The retained song event currently provides text and unlock logic, not a verified staged musical performance. The musical cue and visible response must be designed and reviewed using native assets and supported effects before implementation; do not infer a new Meloetta actor, dance animation or researcher. New concluding dialogue connects the discovery to Stern.
2. Ashen Woods to Ember Path: preserve the Chansey chase and caretaker position. New state-aware caretaker dialogue sends the player along the existing trail. At the roost, use the existing Moltres actor, short restrained quake, cry and battle transition. The resolved state changes the caretaker's response.
3. Institute transport and survey: use existing Institute and elevated-ruins characters, validated arrival anchors and fade transitions. An explicit departure and return conversation makes the transport understandable without a new vehicle sprite. Castform's presence and the Landorus encounter carry the scene.
4. Offshore departure and island sequence: adapt the existing ferry briefing and boarding choreography to Southern Island first, Faraway second. Give Briney short opening and return lines that connect to Peeko and the continuing story. Preserve the Lati sanctuary presentation and Mew chase.
5. Heatran chamber: keep the current chamber and Stone interaction. Supported sound, cry and restrained quake precede the battle; the completion branch conveys that the immediate disturbance has settled. No arbitrary new altar or reward sparkle.
6. Space Center aftermath and Birth Island: change the existing scientist/Steven briefing and return branches so the meteorite lead is established before travel. Preserve the island's triangle movement, palette and Deoxys reveal. No extra encounter is added merely to make the location seem important.
7. Scanner and ruins: give Stern one concrete scanning-result conversation and update the existing ruin inscriptions/dialogue to pay off the player's previous discoveries. Reuse the existing doors, quake and local puzzle effects. The chapter must resolve all designated ruins, not silently finish on opening the first wall.
8. Crisis and origins conclusion: preserve the existing Steven/Wallace staging and Rayquaza choreography. New lines reference discoveries the player has actually completed. Restage existing Origin/Meteor Falls/Steven/Devon interactions to close the opening mystery.
9. Regional map presentation: show the imported destinations, especially Ember Path, under the correct established map naming/icon conventions. A text label in the book is not proof that a map marker is visible or located correctly.

SELECTED EXACT DIALOGUE — PROPOSED EDITORIAL COPY
----------------------------------------------
These lines define tone and the intended connections. They must be placed in the named characters' existing conversations, split into native text boxes and reviewed with the scene. They are not claims about dialogue already implemented.

Devon, after the goods are recovered:
"Those instruments were meant for Captain Stern's surveys. Someone went to a great deal of trouble to stop them reaching him."
"Steven is on Dewford. Take him this letter on your way to Slateport. Perhaps he can tell us what they're looking for."

Steven, Dewford conclusion:
"The account doesn't end here. These travelers followed the same signs out to sea."
"Stern is studying those waters now. Your next delivery may tell us more than this old book can."

Caretaker, after the Ashen Woods rescue:
"Chansey wasn't the only one that came down from the ridge. Something has frightened the Pokémon along Ember Path."
"Follow the old trail. If you reach the roost, give it room."

Ember Path field sequence:
"A rush of hot air sweeps across the path."
"Moltres spreads its wings!"

Wattson, after New Mauville:
"Rotom explains the generator. It doesn't explain the rest of these readings."
"I'll send them to the Weather Institute. You're heading east—speak to the staff when you reach Route 119."

Institute researcher, after the survey:
"Now we can tell the local weather from the disturbance offshore. This is the comparison Aqua tried to take from us."
"Steven is following the old account east. Show him what you saw when your paths meet."

Briney, before the offshore voyage:
"When you brought Peeko home, I promised you a passage. I didn't imagine we'd be going this far!"
"Southern Island first. Then we'll see where that old chart takes us."

Briney, returning from Faraway Island:
"A living piece of the old story. Imagine that."
"The account points to the Orb keepers next. We'll put you ashore near Lilycove. Mt. Pyre is your next stop."

Space Center scientist, after the attack:
"Magma took an interest in more than our fuel. They were studying these meteorite readings."
"The disturbance at Birth Island is still active. We need to know what they were trying to reach."

Stern, after receiving the Scanner:
"The submarine is beneath the southeastern sea, but these old passages send back several echoes. I cannot tell which entrance reaches it."
"The Sealed Chamber account names three surviving route records. We need their directions to pick the right approach. I will mark the way to Pacifidlog and the chamber first."

Wallace, during the crisis:
"The desert warnings. The sea ruins. They were describing this."
"You know where the old account points. We must reach Sky Pillar."

Steven, at the conclusion:
"When we met, you were carrying a letter. Since then, you've stood in the places its authors could only describe."
"The teams thought understanding a Pokémon meant controlling it. You've seen how much they missed."

Mr. Stone, at the conclusion:
"I asked you to make two deliveries. You helped people all across Hoenn."
"Thank you. Now finish the journey you set out to make. The League is waiting."

OUTCOMES AND PRESENTATION CONTRACT
---------------------------------
Required trainer victories are required; defeat/Retry does not mark the chapter complete. Designated required legendary BATTLES resolve on victory or capture; fleeing/loss leaves those battles retryable. C14’s account/song, C26’s investigation, C45’s three ruin puzzles and C48’s two explicit observation interactions have their separately stated non-capture completion actions; their optional legendary battles do not become mandatory by this general rule. Capturing the Pokémon is separate from witnessing/resolving its story scene. A victory without capture must retain an intentional later capture opportunity.

A completed scene stays completed across leaving, returning, saving and reloading. Its monetary reward, physical delivery and optional capture each have their own receipt. Full Bag or PC storage cannot revoke earned travel, duplicate payment, force a repeated boss victory or erase the ability to continue. Castform is the explicit recoverable party entitlement needed for its scene.

Finish the scene before giving control back. Every temporary party, camera state, map effect, movement lock and transport transition must settle on success, failure and cancellation. Use the correct native exits and existing path centers. Do not invent walking routes, actors or sprite frames from prose alone.

Each new/materially restaged sequence requires headless scene execution, screenshots at meaningful moments, and the user's visual review. Check entry, approach, action, battle transition where applicable, each outcome, departure, re-entry and map presentation. A successful build or static coordinate check cannot substitute for viewing the rendered scene.


EXACT LOCAL GUIDANCE FOR MULTI-STEP REQUIRED SCENES
C14: the manor historian points back outside to the meadow warden if the song is missing. The warden points into the manor if its account is unread. Both name Jigglypuff in the manor as a local Sing-capable option and the free Center move service; the performance does not require catching Meloetta.
C26: the archaeologist names the lower chamber of Sandstrewn Ruins, then asks the player to return to this same archaeologist. The required entrance through Mirage Tower's basement must remain usable regardless of optional fossil choice, tower collapse or random appearance. No player is sent to Regirock's Desert Ruins for this earlier chapter. The elevated Route111 ruins reached by C30 transport are a different approach and do not require personal Fly before Winona.
C29/C30: Institute dialogue identifies an owned Castform's custody location, replacement eligibility if none is owned, the party requirement, the transport menu and the return NPC. Neither a full party nor a declined trip removes the return service or makes the player guess how to arrange the party.
C34–C36: first departure runs the ship chapter once, then Southern Island, then Faraway Island. The captain explicitly offers the next destination. Repeated ordinary voyages never require clearing cabins. At each landing the captain names the path inward and remains the return point. First-voyage progression cannot skip the ship chapter solely because an Eon/Old Sea Map permission is already recorded.
C43: the scientist explains that the triangle must be approached in the fewest steps between its successive positions. Extra steps reset puzzle progress. The island's existing triangle interaction repeats this rule on reset. It must not require knowing the vanilla puzzle from a guide. Preserve the native reveal and identify the harbor as the way back after all outcomes.
C44: the existing key trail must communicate that found keys open the numbered locked rooms of this wreck. Inspection text names the room for each key. A room containing the next clue must identify it before the player exits; the final Scanner message names Stern at Slateport Harbor. Do not leave the player with only “someone may want this.”
C45: first explain the Route134 underwater approach and Dig at the Sealed Chamber's rear wall in plain English. Opening the chamber is not completion of the three-ruin chapter. The revealed account names Desert Ruins on Route111, Island Cave on Route105, and Ancient Tomb on Route120. A first-pass suggested route is Desert Ruins → Island Cave → Ancient Tomb; any already-solved local puzzle remains solved.
Desert Ruins: from the rear inscription, move LEFT twice, DOWN twice, then use the native A-button Rock Smash field interaction with a compatible party member.
Island Cave: read the rear inscription, then make one complete lap next to the chamber wall; if the local puzzle resets, the inscription explains the required wall-adjacent lap again. Do not require a real-time waiting puzzle instead.
Ancient Tomb: go to the middle of the chamber and use the native A-button Flash field interaction with a compatible party member.
Each ruin's completion dialogue names the next unfinished site; the final completed site names Seafloor Cavern on Route128. All three research/puzzle completions are required; Regirock/Regice/Registeel ownership is not. The optional Regigigas inscription explicitly labels its three-Regi party requirement as optional.
C46: every handoff names the next actual scene, including Steven/Wallace at the Cave of Origin, Sky Pillar on Route131, Rayquaza at its top and the return to Sootopolis. Bike requirements, if retained on the mandatory approach, must be stated before departure; no paid item or unrelated report is added during the emergency.
C48: complete the explicit observation interaction at each chamber; entering alone is insufficient and both battles are optional. Distinguish the Origin crystal room, Jirachi's deeper Meteor Falls chamber, Steven's Mossdeep house and Devon's Rustboro building from one another. At every substep, the local completion and repeat text names the next. The optional post-Champion Steven exhibition cave must not be described as the required Jirachi destination.


V4 REVIEW — REQUIRED LOCAL HANDOFF CORRECTIONS
Brawly repeats: “Return to Steven in his room inside Granite Cave, northwest of Dewford. You have delivered his letter and earned my badge; speak to him about the Mega Ring.” Steven then gives the manor/meadow direction. If the letter is missing, Brawly names that same Steven interaction first, without claiming the Ring is already earned.

Follow that floor north to its upper-right side passage. In the side chamber, collect the item ball along the north wall, west of the stairs. That is the Magma Stone.” Source route: 4F warp (20,21) → 3F_3R → 2F_3R → 1F, then 1F upper-right warp (31,3) → 2F_2R entry (36,4), item (26,4). The book fixes these authored anchors; rendered navigation must validate the intervening paths and display useful local guidance before any ambiguous fork. If storage prevents pickup, say so and keep the same finite pickup available; do not give a second unrestricted Stone or tell the player it was a boss drop.
Mew chase: Briney’s landing/repeat line and the existing entrance interaction explain: “Mew hides in the long grass and may vanish from sight. Watch the grass for movement. Move to close off its path; when you are beside it, face it and press A.” Reset/failure text repeats this instruction and points back to the captain for return travel. Catching is optional after the designated encounter resolves. Do not require a remembered vanilla minigame solution.
Before the Sealed Chamber, Stern’s practical sea route is: “From Mossdeep, Surf south through Routes 127 and 128, then west along Routes 129, 130 and 131 to Pacifidlog. Heal there before taking the westward currents. Follow Routes 132 and 133 toward the deep-water opening on Route 134; Dive, follow the underwater passage, then surface into the chamber.” The current junctions and approach to the Dive tile require rendered route guidance/validation, not invented untested movement coordinates.
Inside the Sealed Chamber: “Use Dig at this rear wall. Go through the opening and read the far wall in the inner room.” The inner interaction, not merely Dig, opens the distant doors and displays the three site names.
Missing Flash at Ancient Tomb: “Collect the free Flash license from the hiker at Granite Cave’s entrance, northwest of Dewford. Brawly’s badge allows field use. Return here with a compatible Pokémon, stand in the chamber’s middle, and press A.” No paid teaching or occupied battle-move slot is required by licensed field use.
The wreck’s numbered-room/key instructions, Route134 current forks, Seafloor Cavern’s boulder/current route and the deeper Meteor Falls forks must each be checked in the rendered traversal and recorded in this book when any local wording is refined. Fifty authored chapter handoffs are not proof that those internal navigation checks already passed.

NAVIGATION ACCEPTANCE
Run a guide-free route check at every story handoff and relevant dungeon fork. Record the last message shown, destination actually reachable, required capability available, and repeat clue after dismissing text, re-entry, saving/reloading and returning from an optional detour. Also inspect loss/flee/capture/full-storage/reward-already-claimed branches. A chapter fails this requirement if the next action is only evident from a walkthrough, a flag name, a hidden prerequisite, an earlier one-time message or the author's familiarity with vanilla Emerald. These checks are required evidence, not claims that every current script already passes.


18. COHESION CHECKS, LIMITS AND REVIEW
======================================

A book-level consistency pass must check:
- Every required event has reachable prerequisites under the proposed order; no paid item or optional capture secretly blocks it.
- Every trainer cut has the explicit low-value/pacing rationale authorized by the user and preserves necessary dialogue/rewards. The five v4 additions include redundant grunts/reporters; no named boss is removed. Group counts are not confused with actors, variants or actual fights.
- Every selected family has a practical acquisition/evolution path; stone timing includes physical access, not just a map name.
- Every ability engine has an actual user, partner action, compatible item, useful stat and legal timing; no imaginary Mega ability, unsupported move or impossible Commander/Costar slot.
- Every boss has a distinct plan, an alternative when disrupted, and a clear reason for each reserve.
- All item sources agree with the shared policy: field medicine versus in-battle use; held berries versus field consumables; retired PP/EXP/X systems; free gear resale; finite substitutions; berries/soot/BP/Coins.
- A gift does not become pointless after an earlier purchase. A one-time compensation cannot be claimed repeatedly. A research report is independent of storage.
- Repeated copies in old source are not separate authorities. The TXT design, seed data, explicit amendments and unresolved tasks are visibly distinguished.
- Every new/restaged overworld scene has its own pending native screenshot and user-review record.

Implementation acceptance still open: per-encounter chapter/access verification, full native move/ability/form resolution, action execution and strategy quality, practical mandatory-route money/berry traversal, conflicting untouched flavor text, and native combat/visual testing. Preserve the existing habitat roster; the earlier 650–750 range is not a required curation project or quota. This edition makes concrete progress but is not a fully implemented or certified game. Do not manufacture a “pass” by hiding these boundaries.

The supplied ChatGPT Pro audit and the single authorized Astra High full-context review have been consolidated here. Section 26 records the latter’s eight findings and their dispositions. No additional reviewer loop is authorized. Text review does not replace native, pacing, traversal or visual acceptance.

VIAL AND FIXED PP — RETAINED SOURCE BEHAVIOR
First Center acquisition: one charge, capacity one. One field use restores every current party member's HP (including fainted members), persistent status and current PP to the permitted maximum, and consumes one charge. It is unavailable as a manual in-battle restorative.
Center healing refills it to capacity. C24's rescue upgrades capacity to two and fills both on the first successful upgrade; re-entry does not duplicate or downgrade it. Ordinary field medicine saves a return/refill when those charges are spent.
Fixed Champions PP preserves the current source formula: maximum PP = 4 × (floor(base move PP / 5) + 1), except Revival Blessing, Sketch and Struggle retain their declared base PP. Examples: base 5→8, 10→12, 15→16, 20→20, 25→24, 30→28. It is neither universally base PP nor a universal fully-PP-Max multiplier. No permanent PP Up/PP Max investment remains. All player/opponent setup and restoration use this same maximum.

TOOL LIFECYCLE / COMPENSATION
In the printed paid evolution stock, Linking Cord and the Scrolls of Darkness/Waters are reusable key devices; the other listed evolution stones/tools are consumed on a successful applicable evolution. No item is consumed for an invalid target or cancelled use.
Free form stock has explicit lifecycles: DNA Splicers, N-Lunarizer, N-Solarizer, Reins of Unity, Gracidea, Prison Bottle, Rotom Catalog, Zygarde Cube and Reveal Glass are reusable key tools. Adamant Crystal, Griseous Core, Lustrous Globe and the four Genesect Drives are persistent held/form equipment, not manual-use consumables. Pink/Purple/Red/Yellow Nectar is CONSUMED on successful form use and can be replenished freely. No free form item is resale income. Pokémon-specific application conditions still apply. The existing Ring service is the stock-access gate unless a specific later gift overrides it. Reveal Glass is explicitly added after the C29 Institute rescue/gift conversation; its two script labels are first delivery/retry of ONE entitlement.
Rotom Catalog, Prison Bottle and nectar field pickups no longer imply exclusive form access. They are finite demonstrations if needed; if the free service already supplied the item, use one local ten-Ball pack rather than a recurring rebate.
Paid reusable-device compensation applies only to the identified finite Cord/scroll entitlement, not to free field-tool reissues. A second finite rod provider uses the named Ball pack; repeat conversations/reissue never mint cash.
Sea/Lax Incense, Everstone and Soothe Bell are free preparation/breeding/control tools. This preserves their capabilities; corresponding finite pickups now have an explicit demonstration or Ball-pack disposition. Incense is not a paid hidden tax on a breeding route.
Shoal's already-owned first Glalitite exception remains Big Pearl, not the generic duplicate-Mega 3,000.
Other unusual item-specific lifecycle exceptions still require their actual source record, not inference from a name.

SOURCE CHECKS FOR CUSTOM ABILITIES
The configured 7.1 species table confirms: base Electrode/Electric Surge, Blastoise/Mega Launcher, Venusaur/Thick Fat, Pidgeot/No Guard, Wailord/Drizzle, average Gourgeist/Flare Boost (resolve the GOURGEIST alias), Goodra/Poison Heal and Cosmog/Unaware. These are not errors to “fix” with unmodified Showdown legality. They do not establish every move permission in the future merged catalogue.
Mega Malamar retains Contrary. Mega Excadrill has PIERCING DRILL, not Sand Rush. A05/A06/E0408 must deliberately choose base sand-speed or Mega power; speed calculations change on transformation. No post-Mega Sand Rush claim is accepted.
Mega Kangaskhan source stats in HP/Atk/Def/SpA/SpD/Spe order: 105/125/100/60/100/100. Parental Bond's ordinary calculated second-hit modifier is 0.25 in the active generation setting. Already multi-hit/Beat Up handling occurs before Parental Bond. Status, more-than-one-spread-target, two-turn, OHKO, Z-move and Struggle cases are excluded by eligibility. Explicit source bans: Self-Destruct, Explosion, Rollout, Uproar, Endeavor, Ice Ball, Fling, Final Gambit, Dynamax Cannon, Dragon Darts.
This replaces the vague phrase “actual project nerfs”; it does not certify fixed-damage exceptions or every contact/secondary-effect interaction. Those composed cases and future move-pool permissions remain native/catalogue validation tasks.
U0992 zero SpA belongs to the intended useful-IV system; native tests must implement that policy before using zero-IV damage references.

FUNDING RECONCILIATION
Stipends sum to 223,000 including start and C50, 198,000 before C50. The external audit's intended-route subtotal of 107,000 for twenty named protected leader/admin encounters is consistent with the proposed incoming-cap mapping; E0493–E0496 plus E0497 add 76,800. Combined modeled total is 406,800 before purchases, excluding other required/optional battles and loot. This is a design model, not a measured wallet or affordability promise on first arrival.
Do not raise stipends merely because the route cuts look large. First resolve actual fight receipts and the purchase itinerary. Retired encounter income is 20 times the sum of incoming caps for actual removed ordinary fights, not 140 times an invented average.

REMAINING DECISIONS / EVIDENCE
Keep Easy/Medium/Hard as the agreed development level controls. Choosing two final release labels is a later presentation decision after playtesting, not an unassigned mechanic in this implementation specification. Preserve the current 7.1 habitat roster; the watchlist is optional curation rather than a quota. Native matchup performance, actual traversal/marker art and untouched flavor-text conflicts require implementation acceptance. Existing optional activity renewal rules are retained except where the explicit item/economy disposition changes them; no new repeatable money or item entitlement is inferred. Draft 3.1 supersedes the earlier deferral for the eight explicitly amended relationships in section 13. Preserve the already-simplified Finizen/Gimmighoul routes and all other explicit item/location/party/form conditions; do not remove an unreviewed condition by inference.

21. PROTECT CALIBRATION AND HYBRID AI — CENTRAL ACCEPTANCE WORK
=============================================================

STATUS AND PRIORITY
TRAINER DESIGN AND DIFFICULTY PRIORITY — user direction, September 13, 2026: Make the campaign a varied journey through strong, distinctive competitive ideas. Every encounter should earn its place through its theme, memorable Pokemon, capable support/attack composition and an actual working strategy. Weak or rare species can still have meaningful roles. Preserve broad mechanics such as Follow Me, rain, sand, Steam Engine, Storm Drain, Lightning Rod, partner activation and other purposeful synergies. Deliberate no-healing gauntlets are welcome in Gyms, villain encounters and newly authored overworld scenes; overlapping sight lines are not automatically an error. Distinguish ordinary back-to-back encounters, which retain individual victories, from selected explicitly announced endurance challenges, which restart from their first fight after a later-leg loss. The user approved this distinction and granted creative judgment over where each format best serves the game. When a battle or gauntlet is too difficult, the primary balancing tool is a small reduction to one or more individual enemy level offsets, starting with an over-cap or decisive pressure member. Replay each coherent adjustment and use judgment about reasonable difficulty. Do not weaken correct AI, dull a moveset, break a synergy or remove a distinctive Pokemon merely to make a battle easier. Continue fixing real AI/mechanics defects and unsuccessful strategies for their own reasons.

Protect policy is a high-impact shared system: a small scoring mistake can recur across nearly the entire campaign. Its broad moveset presence is not itself a defect and is NOT a percentage-reduction target. Do not solve overuse by stripping Protect from hundreds of builds. Correct the decisions and replace individual move slots only when a better fourth move has a real role.
This section contains the active AI contract and incorporated playthrough repairs. Shared native fixes and bounded battle/timing evidence now exist, but Protect is not certified across the full campaign. Preserve the distinction between an implemented repair, a focused regression, and every-encounter acceptance.

STRONG REFERENCE: EARLY 7.0/7.1 BESPOKE AUTHORING
Reuse the early encounter plans, pair tactics, reviewed sets and native evidence. The located final ledger cutoff is E0118 Kai: 141/516 branches and 110/468 encounter records, with E0119 next. This substantiates the user's “roughly the first 120” reference without inventing 120 completed clean fights or a separate AI engine per encounter.
The same ledger explicitly retains empty/double-guard, repeated-guard, reserve-preservation and timing opportunities. Old ratings are not current proof after roster/cap/format changes. A cut encounter may remain a useful diagnostic fixture without being restored to the campaign.
Historical 7.0 references: docs/trainer_authoring/further_improvements.md and the per-encounter records at source commit 0a43802e498c01dbe6edb10aea7b3d25d1e87324, also preserved in the handoff evidence archive. They describe the old prediction-based forecaster. Current executable owners are the book-derived team strategy/tactic fields and src/battle_ai_pair.c; the current implementation reads committed player commands as specified below. Historical paths are not active instruction documents in the current branch.

ONE HYBRID CONTRACT FOR EVERY TEAM
1. Shared engine: legal actions, current mechanics, damage/status/speed effects, survival, protection success, switching, timers, owner/gimmick limits and knowledge policy.
2. Encounter intent: primary/alternate plan, roles, lead/reserve order, activation prerequisites, who must survive, when a setup is already complete, transformation timing and meaningful fallback.
3. Situational choice: evaluate complete allied action pairs and choose a legal useful line for THIS board. Intent guides evaluation; it does not blindly force “Protect on turn one” or override a losing exchange.
4. Bounded custom hooks: permitted only for a concrete partnership/phase not adequately represented by ordinary intent. Reuse mechanics; do not clone Protect/damage rules into 328 scripts. A hook cannot make an illegal move legal, guarantee a random outcome or bypass the shared counter.
There is one owner for protection mechanics. Global calibration changes do not silently invalidate per-team exceptions; every affected intent/hook must be identifiable.

Native selection legality also applies to a losing board. Reuse the complete current move-limitation mask, including Champions restrictions on spent first-turn attacks, unavailable Spit Up/Last Resort and attacks requiring a lost type. A move that cannot be selected is never a harmless fallback: Joey's 1 HP Pawmi otherwise chose spent Fake Out before an incoming knockout and stalled the actual battle in a selection-error script. Preserve the configured generation rules and legal switch-in resets through the native owner.

INFORMATION CONTRACT — EXPLICIT, NOT THE WORD “OMNISCIENT” ALONE
The user explicitly chose full team/state knowledge PLUS reading the player's already-committed moves and targets on September 12, 2026. This is the intended information mode at every development difficulty. Evaluate the actual committed commands, including the effects of legal move order and target resolution. Do not pretend the player can freely retarget a locked command when evaluating that turn. The mode never grants knowledge of future RNG or an uncommitted future decision.
Native fainted-target fallback is part of that contract. If an earlier action removes the selected opposing recipient, a later single-target attack can hit its surviving partner; switching a weakened reserve into spread damage does not erase the later attack. Resolve eligible Follow Me before this fallback, preserve allied-target failure and Counter-specific rules, and retain the original recipient on branches where it survives. The bounded forecast weights fallback by prior survival rather than declaring uncertain knockouts certain. Correlated spread rolls, item histories and later branches remain approximations, not an exact full battle tree. Brenden's earned rematch exposed this omission; preserve a focused regression for his doomed-reserve switch and for both threatened and unthreatened fallback recipients.
The previous prediction-only paired forecaster is existing implementation evidence, not the v4 information contract. Its alternative-target machinery may remain useful where an action is genuinely unknown, but must not replace known committed player input with an invented alternative. Validate the exact point at which commands become committed and visible; apply the same boundary to normal decisions, switching decisions and the native fixtures. The committed-command mode is implemented in the current native engine and exercised by the earned playthrough. Full-game fairness, robust choice quality and the 1.2-second bound across all relevant boards remain acceptance work.

PROTECT'S VALUE IS THE WHOLE TURN, NOT “THIS MON AVOIDS DAMAGE”
Compare a guarding pair against real attack, support and switch alternatives. Account for:
- actual chance of the shield succeeding, including the shared consecutive-use counter;
- attacks genuinely stopped, actual targets and bypass/Feint/contact behavior;
- the unprotected partner's fate and useful action;
- progress from a timed effect, recovery, item activation or preserved win condition;
- lost damage/support, an opponent's free setup/switch/recovery and wasted friendly weather/terrain/Trick Room turns.
Do not reward the same survival twice under “damage avoided” and “setup preservation.” Protect on one slot does not shield both allies. HP saved on a harmless reserve can be worse than a partner KO. An existing Wish, Speed Boost, poison or Perish clock must actually apply under the current abilities/state before receiving timing credit.

CONSECUTIVE GUARDS AND DOUBLE GUARDS
Use the actual engine success rule; do not create a second hand-coded probability table. Detect/other counter-sharing shields and generation-specific Wide/Quick Guard behavior need their correct distinctions.
Do not forbid every repeated Protect: a low-probability survival attempt can be rational when every other legal line loses. Do not give it a generous generic bonus either.
Both allies guarding is a candidate only with a concrete whole-board payoff, such as a favorable expiring timer or unavoidable damage/status clock. A named payoff merely permits consideration; it does not force double Protect.
Reject empty guard cycles that achieve no useful state change while giving the opponent progress. Repeated same-state guarding must be diagnosable, not hidden by a high win rate against one compliant test team.
The earned first-Gym playthrough exposed a specific endgame pacing failure: a lone Nosepass repeated an ordinary shield with no ally, reserve, recovery or useful clock. A sole remaining Pokemon needs a concrete payoff for even its first passive single-target guard; retaining its HP alone is insufficient. The later earned Laura fight confirmed that an empty first shield can forfeit an available Fake Out knockout. Preserve actual poison/recovery/expiry clocks, committed Sucker Punch denial, an incoming attack spending its final PP, and temporary invulnerability windows. Modern side guards and contact-shield consequences remain distinct. For known human commands, Fake Out is a waiting reason only when the player actually committed Fake Out; merely carrying it does not license an empty double guard.
The earned Takao opening exposed impossible retaliation behind a guarding partner. Counter and Mirror Coat require a preceding qualifying hit on their user in the actual candidate turn, after targeting, redirection and protection. Retaliation follows the latest source in its eligible damage category, with native Follow Me and immunity rules; it does not apply ordinary attack, Helping Hand, weather or screen multipliers to reflected damage. Use incoming damage for single strikes and equal fixed strikes, reflecting only the final strike rather than a multi-hit total. Variable counts and unequal strike sequences retain a limited estimate until their last-hit damage is modeled; do not claim exact correlated roll, miss or multi-hit retaliation simulation. A real Encore lock or Octolock can be useful progress behind a shield even when that turn deals no damage.
Coaching's immediate Attack and Defense effects belong to the complete turn forecast. Its separate future setup preference is credited to the recipient only if it survives the exchange. A flinched recipient can still deserve a boost for next turn when it lives; a flinched recipient facing a certain special knockout cannot. Do not reward a doomed boost merely because the trainer has an authored setup preference.
The earned Roxanne fight also exposed an attack-selection error: a positive isolated knockout/matchup bonus survived even when confirmed Protect blocked that attack. Award positive damage opinions only after a real recipient passes targeting and guard checks, once per move; retain spread damage to an exposed partner and native Protect bypass. Useful chip into the exposed flank must beat an entirely blocked attack.
During every native playthrough battle, explicitly review the cadence of opposing Protect: what each use buys, what attacking/support/switching opportunity it gives up, consecutive-use risk, and whether the fight becomes repetitive without useful progress. The user reiterated this requirement on September 13, 2026. Fix demonstrated pointless, detrimental or excessive guarding in the shared AI or justified individual moveset; do not merely record or excuse it because the trainer remains difficult or eventually loses. A justified individual shield does not establish that the whole fight has good pacing.

TEAM-SPECIFIC EXAMPLES
- Flannery: preserve Torkoal HP only when the partner/action order turns that HP into a useful Eruption line; After You is not valuable after Torkoal already acted.
- Speed Boost users: count the actual speed threshold gained and whether the ability is active; no automatic Protect every time the move is available.
- Norman: Gas suppresses many intended benefits. Guard valuation and reserve entry must use the current mode rather than borrow bonuses from the later psychic phase.
- Coalossal/Weak Armor/Anger Point: a guarded recipient cannot simultaneously receive a damaging ally trigger through an ordinary shield. Compare setup, protection and direct pressure as distinct legal pairs.
- Perish: protecting does not prevent the user's own zero-count faint. A legal switching/trapping plan is required.
- Commander: the hidden partner is not a free second actor. Do not score a two-action guard/setup pattern during the one-attacker phase.
- Choice sets: a useful-looking Protect is not an available escape from an existing lock. Switching and actual move legality govern.
- Contact shields: their real contact consequence can justify a different value from ordinary Protect; do not award poison/damage when no qualifying contact occurs.

SMALL NATIVE ACCEPTANCE MATRIX — REUSE THE EXISTING TOOLS
P01: one Protect genuinely prevents a KO while its partner secures a useful result.
P02: the same apparent self-save loses the unprotected partner; a better attack/switch pair must remain competitive.
P03: both Protect with a real favorable timer/recovery payoff versus an almost identical empty double-guard board.
P04: consecutive Protect/Detect at each relevant counter state; distinguish a rational desperation roll from repeated waste.
P05: Feint, supported bypass abilities/moves, targeted versus spread attacks, and contact-shield consequences.
P06: evaluate the actual committed player moves and targets under the approved information mode; account for native redirection, invalidated targets and action order without inventing a player retarget.
P07: Wish/Speed Boost/status/Perish timing with suppression, immunity, full HP and final-count variations.
P08: friendly weather/terrain/Trick Room about to expire; stalling one's OWN winning window must have a cost.
P09: ally activation and guards, with exact speed/IV/HP/move category and native move order.
P10: one Pokémon left, no useful partner, no useful incoming damage, and ordinary action unavailability.
P11: Encore/Choice lock/PP exhaustion and guards sharing or not sharing success counters.
P12: representative opening, midgame, boss, late-game and optional teams under Easy/Medium/Hard level offsets.
These are distinct failure modes, not a demand for a giant permanent test framework or all combinatorial matchups. Audit the fixture, assumptions and source/ROM identity before changing code or expectations.

Before each native battle, briefly inspect the trainer's current team, authored intent and tactics, and the applicable shared AI code. Look for mechanical bugs, unsupported combinations and weak strategic choices before entering the fight; this is a quick source check, not a replacement for playing it. The user expects a possible quality drop beyond roughly the first 130 previously hand-authored encounters. Improve team composition, movesets, strategies and AI when supported by the encounter evidence, maintaining the canonical book and generated consumers together.
Every Gym trainer is intended as an exceptional difficulty benchmark; Gym leaders should be major challenges beyond their staff. A comfortable win leaving most of the player party untouched warrants an AI and balance audit even if earlier attempts lost. Strong play must have counterplay, but an opening solution should not excuse a passive or tactically broken remainder of the fight. Assess sustained decision pressure, useful enemy actions and resource cost across the full encounter rather than imposing a fixed number of player faints. Inspect flawed AI consequences before compensating with levels; retain individual level tuning when sound choices still yield inappropriate difficulty.

OBSERVABILITY AND CALIBRATION
Record the board and information mode, selected action PAIR, strongest non-guard alternative, guard success probability, relevant predicted/known opponent actions, expected partner consequence, time-window benefit, and the intent that justified the choice. Keep detailed traces in the headless evidence, not player-facing dialogue.
Measure empty opening double guards, repeated guard attempts, genuine beneficial saves, missed protection opportunities, lost setup/partner turns, full-battle pacing and complete decision time. Raw Protect selection rate alone is not acceptance.
Use paired A/B comparisons on the SAME source-bound scenarios, player teams/actions, random seeds and level settings. Broaden only when a change affects more teams or an unresolved concern remains. Neither “remove all Protect” nor a fixed desired guard percentage is an acceptable control policy.
Retain the prior 1.2-second COMPLETE opponent-decision ceiling as the working performance budget, including both actors, switches and forms; target headroom. Host wall time is not automatically cartridge timing. Re-measure after global scoring changes.

READINESS: NO “EVERYTHING ELSE IS PERFECT”
Textual coherence, exact source definitions, executable mechanics, AI decisions, practical difficulty, physical travel and visual presentation are separate evidence.
V4 is the single working specification for agreement and review. It is not release acceptance, and its remaining evidence gaps must stay visible. Still open: full native behavior and information-boundary verification, Protect/other policy calibration, exact roster/cap matchup tuning, late-game pacing, practical acquisition/berry/cash traversal, variable-reward contracts and rendered scene/user acceptance.
A review that finds no new text contradiction does not prove that 1,503 builds are strategically sound. Do not add content to avoid these calibration tasks and do not claim the “hardest game” ambition has been achieved.

Reserves & disruption: Psychic Terrain can block Incineroar's Fake Out against grounded opposing targets; the fact that it is the team's own terrain does not exempt that attack. Magearna's Soul Heart and Mega transition are explicit.
Counterplay & audit: Terrain replacement, Dark/Steel/Fire pressure, spread damage and Haze. Disposition: Keep as optional advanced Wally; include an own-terrain/Fake Out negative test.

T338 — E0499-B01
First two useful turns: Sableye chooses Fake Out/Quash/Encore for a useful Mienshao attack; turn two pivots only when Regenerator and the replacement improve the board.
Alternate deployment: Sableye's control supports Scarf Typhlosion's execution-time Eruption pressure.
Reserves & disruption: Gliscor has an independent Swords Dance/Poison Heal mode, Xurkitree special Electroweb pressure and Mega Zeraora a physical finish. Plasma Fists' conversion can affect later same-turn Normal attacks.
Counterplay & audit: Priority denial, Dark target restrictions, Water/Ground pressure and speed reversal. Disposition: Keep; source-bound Mega Zeraora and current-HP Eruption matter more than merely listing rare species.

T339 — E0500-B01
First two useful turns: Gigalith establishes sand while Sandslash attacks under Sand Rush; turn two uses the weather window or transitions to support only when it protects a worthwhile attacker.
Alternate deployment: Clefable's Follow Me supports Necrozma's special pressure and reactive Weakness Policy.
Reserves & disruption: Whimsicott's Tailwind is a backup/contested-speed tool, not automatic redundancy. Rotom-Wash offers burn/coverage and may take sand chip.
Counterplay & audit: Weather replacement, Taunt, Wide Guard, Water/Grass pressure and Haze. Disposition: Keep; redirection may correctly prevent rather than enable a Policy trigger, so don't score both benefits at once.

T340 — E0501-B01
First two useful turns: Cresselia sets Trick Room or helps a useful Volcanion attack according to the opposing speeds. Turn two spends room turns instead of cycling unnecessary recovery.
Alternate deployment: Scrafty's Fake Out can protect Cresselia's initial room action before a deliberate Mega.
Reserves & disruption: Mawile is base Intimidate, not a second Mega; Slurpuff supplies Sweet Veil support, Celesteela Wide Guard/physical pressure. No rain setter is present.
Counterplay & audit: Taunt, competing slower teams, special pressure, Water/Fire immunity and targeted attacks around Wide Guard. Disposition: Keep; precise base-to-Mega abilities and the slow-mode Speed values must be explicit.

T341 — E0504-B01
First two useful turns: Liepard's Fake Out/Taunt/Encore supports Fezandipiti's attack or Tailwind; turn two converts the control into damage rather than introduce another passive support.
Alternate deployment: Mesprit's Helping Hand/speed control supports Eternal Floette's Mega/Calm Mind pressure.
Reserves & disruption: Alolan Persian and Incineroar are pivot reserves, not an automatic double-support lead. Toxic Chain remains probabilistic and Wish has a specific delayed recipient.
Counterplay & audit: Taunt, priority denial, Steel/Poison/Ground pressure and burst damage before setup. Disposition: Keep optional at live cap 60 on the main voyage; the old level-100 ship floor is discarded.

T342 — E0505-B01
First two useful turns: Manectric attacks or uses Snarl/Volt Switch according to the Choice Scarf lock while Lapras attacks or establishes a useful snow state. Turn two evaluates the actual post-Mega ability and weather.
Alternate deployment: Luxray's Intimidate/Snarl supports Clawitzer's special Launcher pressure.
Reserves & disruption: Lightning Rod can intercept friendly single-target Electric moves from Luxray; it does not make all Electric attacks safe or effective.
Counterplay & audit: Ground/Grass/Fighting pressure, weather replacement and Choice-lock exploitation. Disposition: Keep as optional ship content; bind Mega Lapras's actual ability before claiming a snow payoff beyond the listed move.

T343 — E0506-B01
First two useful turns: Weavile's Ice Shard may hit Armarouge only when the resisted physical damage and Defense drop are worth the Speed gain; Armarouge must not Protect through that trigger. Turn two uses actual speed and survival, not an imagined Policy boost.
Alternate deployment: Weavile's Fake Out supports Scarf Genesect's immediate special pressure without friendly damage.
Reserves & disruption: Mega Scolipede is a separate timed transformation/Speed Boost reserve. The active ally-hit line does not depend on Dynamax or Tera.
Counterplay & audit: Fake Out/priority denial, redirection where supported, physical pressure into lowered Defense and speed reversal. Disposition: AMEND CANDIDATE: zero Weavile's Attack IV to reduce activation damage, accepting weaker Knock Off; native survival/order tests remain required.

T344 — E0507-B01
First two useful turns: Miltank uses Helping Hand only for a relevant Tauros attack or attacks itself; turn two may bring Primeape for anti-drop pressure.
Alternate deployment: Miltank and Primeape are the alternate direct physical mode.
Reserves & disruption: Cosmog's two-move set and custom Unaware are a deliberate novelty cost, not a secretly powerful competitive role. Teleport requires an available legal receiver and spends the action.
Counterplay & audit: Fighting pressure, Taunt, special attacks and physical mitigation without feeding Defiant. Disposition: Keep optional novelty, but flag Cosmog's unusual attack legality/form role for source validation rather than declare a complete high-pressure quartet.

T345 — E0509-B01
First two useful turns: Tsareena attacks or pivots while Salazzle uses Fake Out only when it buys a useful action; turn two can introduce Darkrai after a safe opening.
Alternate deployment: Salazzle's Fake Out supports Darkrai's Nasty Plot or a risk-bearing Hypnosis.
Reserves & disruption: Overqwil supplies Intimidate/coverage. Queenly Majesty protects the side from specified opposing priority, not from all disruption, and Mega Darkrai may change its base ability.
Counterplay & audit: Spread damage, Taunt, Fire/Flying/Psychic pressure and sleep immunity. Disposition: Keep optional ship content; do not credit Hypnosis as guaranteed setup protection.

T346 — E0510-B01
First two useful turns: Kyogre attacks while Therian Tornadus sets Tailwind only when needed or applies pressure. Turn two uses a real Regenerator switch when the replacement improves the board.
Alternate deployment: Base Calyrex's Helping Hand supports physical Mega Mewtwo X; it is not a fused rider form.
Reserves & disruption: Arceus is ordinary Normal without a plate, and Terapagos requires an explicit non-Tera form contract. Tera Starstorm's name alone neither permits Tera nor proves the set illegal.
Counterplay & audit: Weather replacement, Wide Guard, priority denial, physical/special mitigation and targeting the actual support. Disposition: Keep optional postgame status; bind Terapagos's supported form and move behavior before acceptance, with no invented fusion or Tera mechanics.

T347 — E0511-B01
First two useful turns: Ninetales supplies sun while Kangaskhan uses Fake Out or immediate pressure; turn two may pivot to the appropriate support/threat pair.
Alternate deployment: Chlorophyll Tangrowth's Rage Powder supports Mega Mewtwo Y's special offense.
Reserves & disruption: Gengar supplies Icy Wind and Zeraora physical coverage. Plasma Fists can alter a later same-turn Kangaskhan Double-Edge, and Tangrowth's powder has normal target restrictions.
Counterplay & audit: Weather replacement, powder immunity, Dark/Ground pressure, priority denial and special mitigation. Disposition: Keep existing Altering Cave staging and live-cap scaling; no old fixed level-100 floor or automatic second Mega.

T348 — E0512-B01
First two useful turns: Skarmory chooses Tailwind only when Rayquaza's attack or safe Dragon Dance benefits; turn two attacks through the window or enters the appropriate heavy reserve.
Alternate deployment: Cradily's Storm Drain supports Melmetal's physical pressure against eligible single-target Water attacks.
Reserves & disruption: Dialga supplies special coverage, and Metagross is the proposed sole Mega designation. Rayquaza's move-based eligibility must not accidentally create a second Mega for the same owner.
Counterplay & audit: Ground/Fire/Fighting pressure, Wide Guard where relevant, ability suppression and special attacks into the physical core. Disposition: AMEND CANDIDATE: designate Mega Metagross and keep Rayquaza untransformed; optional exhibition only, never a C48 research gate.

T349 — E0513-B01
First two useful turns: Roserade attacks or uses legal Sleep Powder while Togekiss redirects a meaningful single-target threat. Turn two should bring a stronger attacker when the support pair cannot make progress.
Alternate deployment: Togekiss supports Miraidon's special pressure after the deliberate Electric Terrain transition.
Reserves & disruption: Electric Terrain can make Sleep Powder fail against grounded targets, including targets of the team's own Roserade. Spiritomb, mixed Scarf Lucario and Mega Garchomp Z provide distinct reserve roles.
Counterplay & audit: Terrain replacement, powder immunity, Ground/Fairy pressure, Taunt and special mitigation. Disposition: AMEND CANDIDATE: keep Roserade's sleep phase and Miraidon's terrain phase mutually explicit; source-bind custom Mega Garchomp Z rather than import ordinary Mega stats.

V4 DISPOSITIONS OF REVIEW GATES
The layout questions in G03 are answered by the source-bound formation contracts above; actual native execution remains required. G07 uses the user's newly approved committed-command information mode, superseding the older undecided/prediction-only wording. G02's missing flat catalogue is supplied in section 23; verify that expansion against the native factory during implementation. The other gates remain validation work, not presumed passes.
The earlier economy/preparation/scene implementation has scoped native and headless evidence. That evidence does not certify this trainer candidate, selected-command AI, the v4 sequential story gates, every guide-free handoff, or a fresh full-game release. The one-time Astra High review is complete; section 26 records its findings and dispositions.


23. REGIONAL STARTERS AND EXACT GENERATED RIVAL SETS
===================================================

This closes the flat regional-export gap identified by the supplied trainer audit. Data is expanded from the current default Doubles catalogue and the actual opening/regional factory overrides; it is source-derived, not a new native battle test. All nine generation choices and all three starter families are represented. The player chooses two different starters within the selected generation. The remaining family belongs to the rival; character gender only chooses the presentation alias.

Player opening P records below apply to either selected starter at level 5, IVs all 31. The pre-preparation rescue opponents are bespoke level 2 Poochyena and Zigzagoon, not live-cap-scaled ordinary trainers. Poochyena: Focus Sash, Rattled, Jolly, V001, Crunch/Play Rough/Sucker Punch/Helping Hand. Zigzagoon: Sitrus Berry, Gluttony, Adamant, V001, Belly Drum/Extreme Speed/Seed Bomb/Protect. No extra cap or stipend follows this rescue. Player acquisitions later obey the normal cap policy.

For rivals, the E/B party below remains the full party definition: replace ONLY the listed Hoenn starter slot with the chosen generation's corresponding R record at the same evolution stage. Keep all other U members, their order, offsets and owner-level permissions. Use the explicit R held item/moves/ability/nature/EVs, IV31 and friendship255. Hoenn generation 3 uses its authored U set directly, including its encounter-specific item and moves; it is not regenerated from this table. There are 72 non-Hoenn stage records (24 starter families × three stages), not 72 extra canonical encounters. Stage is determined by the E party's authored starter stage, not by an automatic evolution at a different cap. R family ordering is Grass, Fire, Water within a generation.

No Item Clause applies to the campaign. A shared Eviolite or Sitrus across partners is permitted. Mega access still requires the native species/item/form mapping and the one-per-owner battle limit; an inherited slot permission does not create a nonexistent Mega or authorize another member by accident. The default catalogue may depend on weather without the team owning a setter: that is an explicit tactical weakness for review, not an assumed automatic field effect. These are the exact inherited candidates; the AI must still choose useful weatherless moves.

24. THE HAND-AUTHORED 7.0 AI AND BATTLE PACING
=============================================

REVIEW SCOPE AND WHAT SURVIVES
The source is the actual 7.0 release commit 0a43802e49. The first 100 reviewed encounter groups span E0001–E0107 because the ID sequence has deliberate gaps and some groups have multiple owner records. There are 111 individual final-stat review documents in that span. The later complete ledger reaches E0118, 110 groups and 141/516 branches. Those are historical scoped-review counts, not a claim that this new game has passed 100 battles.

The current isolated checkout's src/battle_ai_pair.c and src/battle_ai_switch_items.c match the 7.0 versions byte for byte. The inspected main-AI difference removes an unused dynamic-function setter, not the paired decision logic. Trainer-plan table changes include the already-authorized campaign cuts. The new book has not replaced your authored AI with an unrelated implementation.

The practical work is directly useful. Preserve the distinction between a move's presence, a staged valid partnership, an actually selected action pair, and a complete multi-turn strategy. Preserve exact Speed/HP tradeoffs only when the new live levels, IV policy and roster still satisfy them. New committed-player-input knowledge changes the information available; re-evaluate the decisions under that mode instead of applying all old heuristic constants unquestioningly.

CONCRETE LESSONS CARRIED INTO V4
1. Establish, exploit and fallback belong together. After speed control or activation, cash in the advantage; do not repeatedly set up or guard because the opening move once scored well.
2. Cristian's Falinks must precede its Justified recipient and survive long enough to activate it. Count actual eligible Beat Up donors, allied damage and redirection. Direct attacks remain valid when they win immediately. Recheck its finely separated Speed values under the v4 offsets.
3. Joey's protected Belly Drum needs Clefairy to survive and the boosted priority to produce a payoff. A successful setup action alone is insufficient evidence.
4. A useful Tailwind must change a living partner's actual move order or support a usable Wind Power benefit. It cannot earn value from fainted targets, an unusable Electric move, or opponents that the relevant attackers already outrun.
5. Do not reverse your own useful Trick Room when both setters can choose it. Preserve backup setters for disruption and later restoration; the same pair must consider both actions together.
6. Guard value is the entire turn. Preserve Allen's legitimate Wide Guard against actual spread pressure, while avoiding an empty double-Protect opening when Fake Out plus a productive switch is better. Preserve Wish, Orb, Speed Boost and Perish controls alongside negative empty-wait cases.
7. The historical repeated-guard commitment margin of 35 is a heuristic with bounded evidence, not part of the battle rules. Do not canonize that scalar or remove it without understanding the demonstrated behavior. V4 requires rational desperation rolls and opportunity-cost evaluation under the correct native probability.
8. Pollen Puff, Life Dew and Heal Pulse have different ally-target and protection interactions. Do not swap them because all appear to be healing moves. Preserve the repaired native Pollen Puff path and the historical rejected Heal Pulse-through-Protect proposal.
9. A manual switch spends that slot's action. Regenerator recovery, Intimidate recycling, Costar copying, First Impression reuse and delayed Mega all need a real entry and a subsequent useful position. A staged reserve snapshot is not proof of natural switch selection.
10. Preserve the no-bench pivot cleanup repair. Hit-and-run moves, Parting Shot and Palafin re-entry must not claim a switch or Hero payoff without a legal reserve. Hidden Commander Tatsugiri is not a second acting battler.
11. Base and Mega ability windows matter. Wattson's reserve Manectric can preserve Lightning Rod; Shawn's Acid Spray must precede the relevant Ampharos attack; a Mega label does not justify losing a currently essential support ability.
12. A move that is already ineffective must not masquerade as safe defense: repeated status into an already affected/immune target, Leech Seed into revealed redirection, or hazards aimed at the wrong side cannot get phantom progress. Preserve the native repairs and their negative controls.
13. Trainer friendship is authored: Return255 and the specific Frustration0 users. Preserve meaningful zero-IV exceptions separately; old all-31 calculations are not proof of new ally-activation damage.
14. Do not replace an unusual support Pokémon with a generic powerful attacker merely to improve a rating. Paras, Milcery, Lickitung and other specialists were chosen for actual partnerships. Repetition is judged by role and nearby encounter experience, not species frequency alone.
15. Preserve rejected experiments and observed losses as lessons. Bulking every mon, adding Helping Hand everywhere or forcing setup did not reliably improve outcomes. The goal is a coherent difficult encounter with executable counterplay, not a perfect-looking spreadsheet or inflated win claim.
16. Measure complete decision time including cold setup, both actors, switching and forms. Historical samples around 31–71 GBA frames include narrow headroom; 7.0's first-Mega improvement from 89 to 60 frames is a scoped result, not a universal maximum. Keep the 1.2-second complete-decision budget and target headroom.

BATTLE PACING — DESIGN OWNER
The user's reported experience is that difficult doubles, including Protect turns, can take roughly two to ten times as long as vanilla battles. This is a planning observation, not a measured universal multiplier. Judge total player time: decision latency, useful battle turns, text/animations, retries, forced fight density and distance between recovery points. Merely removing seconds of AI calculation does not solve a long redundant encounter.

The single review has been integrated: 324 active groups, 369 party definitions and 342 distinct trainer battles are the implementation baseline. The five additional retired fights are listed in section 8. The earlier 140-group cut was not an untouchable quota. Further removal, consolidation or a carefully placed new encounter is authorized when its purpose is explicit. Do not insert a battle merely because a new map needs activity; the Moltres, Heatran, island and ruin scenes already supply events. No additional grunt ambush is prescribed by v4 just to make those locations feel important.

Every retained encounter must justify at least one distinct contribution: story consequence, a new or meaningfully advanced doubles lesson, a memorable character/boss identity, or a worthwhile optional challenge/reward. Ordinary route fights that repeat the same lesson without adding a meaningful decision are the first removal candidates. Preserve important Gym personnel, major rivals, leaders/admins and the League by default; improve their pacing and cooperation rather than deleting their identities. Low-value fights do not become acceptable solely because substantial authoring time was spent on them.

The first 100-group review shows why neither blind preservation nor blanket deletion is right: nearby teams can share a species while teaching very different roles, and some elaborate teams still spend turns on weak follow-through. Use the exact coaching and open opportunity records above when deciding which encounter earns its time.

Pacing hotspots after the single review, to verify in complete native chains:
- Museum: retain E0050 then Archie E0052, ten opposing Pokémon across two battles. E0051’s battle is retired and its actor/dialogue retained. Follow the field-control/recovery contract below; individual opening samples are not full-chain proof.
- Meteor Falls/Mt. Chimney: retain E0127’s supported two-owner battle, one sun grunt, Tabitha and Maxie. The second E0130 grunt fight is retired. Test the actual joint plan and complete chain rather than substituting two same-owner leads or deleting a named boss.
- Route116/Route117 and ash routes: preserve distinctive activation, support and disruption lessons, but inspect clusters and optional positioning. A new player's main route must not accidentally trigger several unrelated doubles because adjacent actors were misclassified.
- Space Center: preserve the Steven team-up as the climax. Grunt 6/E0406 is retired; grunt 5 and grunt 7 remain required legs with field control between them. Tabitha and the final joint fight remain distinct encounters.
- Ship: all five retained passenger fights stay optional, with healing available. Boarding and onward travel never demand a cabin-clear flag.
- Wreck/ruins/late caves: puzzle navigation and capture scenes already cost time. Do not pad every chamber with another six-member trainer or mandate captures to extend the route.

Protect stays when it produces a useful decision: preserving an attacker while its partner acts, buying a genuine timer/recovery turn, countering a known target, or taking the only remaining survival chance. A lone last Pokémon must also justify its first guard; preserving an unchanged position while forfeiting a guaranteed priority knockout is not a payoff. Empty repeated guard cycles, setup after the advantage is already secured, and support without a usable recipient are defects to correct. Never impose a desired Protect percentage or remove all defensive play to make the clock shorter.

Authoring acceptance: every battle has an explicit purpose and actual party plan; every compulsory chain has its fight order and recovery conditions stated; additions name the exact location/actor/staging and retain the visual review requirement. Runtime acceptance after implementation records full-chain turns, losses/retries and elapsed play time under representative player choices, with complete AI time reported separately. There is no invented universal battle-duration limit and no claim that the 342-fight count already achieves ideal pacing.


COMPULSORY CHAINS, RECOVERY AND RETRY — SETTLED V4 CONTRACT
Every chain has an explicit order, recovery boundary and restart rule. The field-separated story rows below currently return control between legs and announce the next opponent before starting it. These rows are not a ban on deliberate endurance encounters: the user welcomes well-authored, tested no-healing gauntlets in story and overworld content as well as optional challenges. Do not automatically separate a difficult existing chain before assessing its purpose and playing it as a whole. The player may use ordinary out-of-battle medicine/Vial and currently available preparation tools, or retreat to an existing Center/PC and return. There is no automatic free between-leg heal/refill unless the row below names one. Progress through already-defeated story legs persists; leaving does not require replaying them or pay their first-clear rewards again. The next leg starts through the existing relevant character interaction, with a repeatable direction to it. Inside one actual battle, normal doubles rules and available participants apply; a last surviving player flank is not converted into a singles battle.
For field-separated story legs, Retry restores the exact CURRENT LEG checkpoint, including that leg’s incoming HP/status/PP/items and party arrangement. An explicitly designated no-healing gauntlet instead restarts the complete attempt from its first fight after a loss or retry, with the first-fight party checkpoint; a later-leg retry must not bypass the earlier fights. Field resources spent before that checkpoint remain spent. A player who wants to heal or rebuild chooses to leave the battle rather than accepting an unwinnable damaged retry forever; ordinary defeat returns them to recovery without cash punishment. No chain restart or aborted attempt creates duplicate prize/stipend/reward receipts.

Entry checks cannot softlock a required chain with one healthy Pokémon: field control and an explicit route to recovery remain available before a fresh leg. Native one-flank continuation remains valid within an ongoing battle and wherever the retained entry command deliberately permits it. Steven’s special selection requires three healthy non-Egg Pokémon after his offered heal. The chosen control boundaries are v4 design changes where the old scripts dispatched several battles without releasing control; historical 7.0 no-heal/no-control chains are not the current authoring authority.

25. EVERY-ENCOUNTER NATIVE DOUBLES TESTING AND SHAREABLE EVIDENCE
================================================================

USER REQUIREMENT
Every retained authored trainer encounter must receive actual native doubles testing and an individual review of its intended strategy. Compilation, valid-looking sets, random automatic victories and a sampled subset of trainers cannot satisfy this requirement. The existing E identifiers, branch IDs and tactic identities remain the common index for the book, native parties, test selection, traces and reports; do not replace the user's authoring work with an unrelated numbering scheme.

PLAY AND BEAT THE GAME — LATEST USER PRIORITY
The earned fresh-save campaign is the main implementation and verification path. Catch and prepare Pokemon through the game, fight every retained authored trainer as it is reached, develop the hybrid AI through those native fights, and continue through the Champion. Interact with NPCs for story, directions, rewards, acquisition and useful services. Build the agreed missing story/overworld content when progression reaches it, then play through the result. Preserve the book's full adventure scope; do not replace it with a narrow test route.

CAPTURE FLOW AND OBSERVATION CONTRACT: The native campaign must retain the normal Pokédex, nickname and full-party swap/PC choices. Only explicitly synthetic automatic-capture fixtures may skip those menus. Leaving the nickname or party/PC Yes/No prompt clears its window before subsequent delivery text. Capture telemetry records the actual native delivery result and verifies ownership; it never chooses a destination or changes capture odds. During the C13 Granite Cave continuation, Carbink and Prankster Sableye were caught by ordinary Great Ball rolls and stored in the PC. Their archived capture flow exposed a native-mode full-party prompt bypass and an uncleared Yes/No overlay. Both are being repaired; those earlier catches prove acquisition, not acceptance of the repaired menu branches. Keep baseline/fixed visual evidence and earned capture provenance distinct.

C13 NATIVE CONTINUATION: Cristian was defeated on the third earned attempt in 13 turns after two archived eight-turn losses. Prankster Sableye was caught in Granite Cave B1F, withdrawn through the PC, prepared with the Center's Prankster Quash set, and raised with the Leveler. Only Sableye survived, at 48/76 HP; the five other party members fainted. No enemy level, team or move was weakened. The run now has 34 unique trainer clears; Jocelyn and Brawly remain ahead. All 13 measured opposing decisions were at most 51 native frames including setup (about 0.85 seconds). This is sampled timing, not full-game acceptance. Protect on the opening pair and later Falinks/Annihilape had observable defensive value. The final Choice Band Dynamic Punch lock left Machamp unable to damage Sableye. Diagnosis found that the pair forecast omitted a newly inflicted burn's immediate physical-damage reduction, which can falsely predict a knockout and preserve a doomed partner in the forecast. The archived win remains earned evidence, not acceptance of that defect.

TIMELY BURN FORECAST: An ordinary legal Will-O-Wisp must reduce the target's remaining physical attack in the same turn, after priority, redirection, protection and accuracy are resolved. A late burn never weakens an already executed attack, and an earlier newly inflicted status prevents a second status. Use the existing bounded effect branch rather than future RNG or a new search tree. Do not award the reduction against status/type/ability/priority immunity, reflected status, an immediate cure berry, or unmodeled status-benefit interactions (Guts, Facade, Quick Feet, Flare Boost, Marvel Scale, Synchronize). Those special interactions retain their existing single-action opinion pending dedicated forecasts. This scope covers immediate damage, not a new residual-burn/endgame solver. A focused native regression must distinguish a partner saved by Protect after a timely burn from an unneeded Protect when the physical knockout still occurs. The regression passes seven native cases: timely burn, no burn, late burn, Guts, Water Veil, Lum Berry and Facade. Existing Coaching and Brenden fainted-target cases also pass. The retrospective source audit covers all 34 currently cleared trainer IDs: each uses the shared smart doubles evaluator. Trainer plan/tactic modifiers do not implement a separate burn-damage calculator. Relevant earlier exceptions include Roxanne, both May branches played, Laura, Johnson and Brenden (Guts/Facade); Cindy and Josh (Lum Berry). Jerry and Josh themselves carry Will-O-Wisp. Existing burn damage already uses the native damage routine; the repaired gap is newly inflicted same-turn burn. This is code-path and focused native coverage, not 34 replayed victories or complete status-benefit forecasting. For every future shared AI defect, identify affected earlier trainers, inspect applicable bespoke tactics, and run bounded behavioral checks where their mechanics could share the defect; preserve original earned results and label retrospective evidence honestly.
